analysts.summary:
Saint Alessia hosted a 0.73.79 TESTER run (runtime 0.32.23, hash 6844d4f8) from 09:52 to 12:07, 5 players, rounds 1-32 (2:02:22). dukka and OdyDio joined in the lobby. Rapt0r linked at 10:05:16 (round 2) and was in the mission at 10:08:25; the 90 s join hold timed out at 10:06:47 before that. Aquila linked at 11:27:50 (round 24). Nobody dropped mid-run and no host migration happened. Specials: r4 shuttle, r8 Spaceport, r13 MINDRIPPER, r19 Alicorn, r23 amphibious, r26 MINDRIPPER, r30 VALKA. Ace rounds: r16, r22, r25, r28, r31. Every special and ace round completed and was cleaned up. Downs and revives: dukka down 4x, Rapt0r 2x, the host 1x; 6 revives (2,600 to 13,890 Z). The host paused and quit at round 32's start (12:04:58, a clean teardown-gate exit). The co-op leaderboard run was ACCEPTED (200), but at 209,700 against the 214,200 shown locally, because the Worker doesn't know the 'valka' special.

Most important NEW finding: after the Alicorn round (unit removed 11:03:33), the host and the joiners kept the Alicorn parked pools' 131 addresses in SPC.alcnPool. hostPlane/clientPlane then skipped any new enemy plane allocated at one of those freed addresses. Before the removal: 50 hunt orders, 0 short flights, 3 rs (all at joins). After it: 18 of 41 hunts were short, and 62 rs|j answers went out in 18 waves, each to every joiner, about every 3 minutes until the end. Rapt0r's log shows the first stray ever 3 minutes after the removal, then 86 copies torn down as strays. This is the concrete 'desync from around wave 20' the players reported. It is still open at HEAD (sv_coop.lua:505 / :1154).

Perf: the host tick went 14.2 ms (r1-7), 52.6 (the r8 Spaceport window), 58.3 (r10-19), 63.5 (r20-31). Host fps went from about 37 to about 24. The cost of an SV_UnitAlive call tracked the units spawned: 0.68 ms at 3 units, 1.85 at 17, 4.14 at 49 (the Spaceport put 32 units on the list at round 8, and they were never recycled), and 7.1 at 88. It was 35 of the 63.5 ms late. This host reached R30's late-run cost 10 rounds earlier.

What 0.73.80 changed against what grew: LANDW targets the 3,818 airfield-window walks (149 s). But ALIVE covers only the rounds' and the Spaceport's calls; the allies' counts, airUp (twice a second), the leave probe and the director still call SV_UnitAlive raw at HEAD. Its 8 asks/s floor at 7 ms is itself about 14 ms a tick. The native linear scan is unchanged. Other new items: the Worker lacks 'valka'; the pay audit logs special pays before the co-op split (about 2x); the Alicorn VLS 'found by a search' line appeared (subclass name mismatch); the migration ranking is re-sent and logged 719 times. No Lua error, no crash, and the native guards caught 0 faults.

findings.title: After the Alicorn round, new enemy planes at the parked pools' freed addresses get no co-op id: partly bound flights, strays and a resync wave every ~3 min to the end of the run
findings.sessions: a_31round host (0.73.79 TESTER); cross-checked against b_Logs Rapt0r (his clock = host +2:00:00, from matching jn times, e.g. host crumb 11:16:13 vs his 13:16:12)
findings.evidence:
Host Lua log. The Alicorn spawned 11:00:47; 'the Alicorn's pooled aircraft: 131 put away' (lines 6718-6719); its unit 'removed (SV_Recycle: 1)' at 11:03:33 (6877).

BEFORE the removal (10:02-11:03): 50 hunt orders 'ERA_Unit_N_Dep_AirN goes after player N's real plane (N planes ordered onto it)', 0 with fewer planes than the flight (Air0=2, Air1=4, Air2=6). Only 3 'asked for the whole picture: sent (rs|j)' crumbs, all at joins.

AFTER it: 41 hunts, 18 short. Examples: 11:06:08 ERA_Unit_02_Dep_Air1 '1 planes' (a 4-ship, line 7241); 11:16:52 ERA_Unit_02_Dep_Air2 '2 planes'. That second flight is a 6-ship: native 11:16:46 'spawn ERA_Unit_02_Dep_Air2: up, 6 aircraft', and Lua logged six 'AI aircraft created' k0-k5 at 11:16:47. There were 62 rs|j asks in 18 waves (every linked joiner each time; sizes 3,3,...,4; median 175 s apart) from 11:06:20 to 12:02:25. Each wave re-sent 20-30 flights per joiner ('sent player N the run: 26 flights'). The R30 run (same build, no Alicorn round) had 8 rs in 2 h.

Rapt0r's log: the first stray of his whole run is at 13:06:21 = host 11:06:21: 'ERA_Unit_02_Dep_Air1 #2, #3, #4' (his line 4388), i.e. the host's 1-of-4 flight. He had 47 stray events with 86 copies taken down unpaid, and 53 flights partly bound, e.g. 13:17:08 'ERA_Unit_02_Dep_Air2 here: 2 of 6 planes bound to the host's (spawned as gen 264; the host's last ids for it: 2 for gen 264)' (4906). His strays are all '#ord' copies (never a 'BP_' name) and skew to the high ords (#4 x27, #6 x14, #2 x19, #1 x5), which is what compacted host ords produce.
findings.fix:
Check the set only for the Alicorn's own unit. At sv_coop.lua:505 and :1154: `if unit == "SV_Unit_Alicorn" and SPC.alcnPool and a and SPC.alcnPool.set[a] then return end`. Its pools always arrive with that unit: SPC.alicornPooled requires unit == UNIT.

Also set SPC.alcnPool = nil when the Alicorn's unit is removed (where 'the Alicorn's unit ... removed (SV_Recycle: 1)' is logged) and in LEVEL_DROPS.

Add a coop_ground_test case: after the Alicorn's removal, a pool flight's plane whose address was a pool's gets its 'bd' and is bound on the joiner.

verdicts.reason:
I re-checked the evidence in the logs and code, and it holds.

**The hunt orders change at the Alicorn's removal.** In the host's Lua log there are 91 "goes after player N's real plane" lines.
- Before 11:03:33 there are 50, and none is short of its flight's size: Air0 2 x34, Air1 4 x11, Air2 6 x5. That includes hunts held 51-70 s by Wolf traps.
- After 11:03:33 there are 41, and 18 are short. 15 of those 18 came only 5-7 s after the spawn, so kills can't explain them. Examples: 11:06:08 ERA_Unit_02_Dep_Air1 "1 planes" (line 7241, spawned 11:06:02); 11:16:52 ERA_Unit_02_Dep_Air2 "2 planes" (8289).
- The native log has that second flight at 11:16:46 "up, 6 aircraft". Lua logged six "AI aircraft created" lines, k0-k5, with the unit (8272-8278), and there is no "coop: plane error" anywhere.

**The host sent fewer ids than it had planes.** Rapt0r's line 4906 (13:17:08, his clock is the host's +2 h) reads "2 of 6 planes bound ... the host's last ids for it: 2 for gen 264". That count comes from the joiner's "bd" handler, `bl.n`. So the host sent only 2 ids for 6 planes.

**Only the address check can drop them.** In hostPlane (0.73.79 at 1717cef, sv_coop.lua:462-466) the only exits before `send("bd")` are `not u` and `SPC.alcnPool.set[a]`. `u` exists, since 2 ids were sent. The wrapper (1717cef :4222-4225) calls hostPlane under the same conditions as rawLogPlane, which logged all six. So 4 of the 6 typhoons had addresses in the set.

That set only gets addresses from SPC.alicornPooled, which requires unit == "SV_Unit_Alicorn" and a pool name (sv_alicorn.lua:107-115). It is reset only by the next alicornSpawn (:60): nothing sets it to nil, and there is no LEVEL_DROPS entry. So the Alicorn's freed pool planes' addresses were reused by new planes.

**The timing matches.** The native log destroyed the Alicorn's unit actor at 11:04:03 (line 1515). The flights spawned at 11:03:36-59, before that, got full hunts (11:03:48 2/2, 11:03:54 4/4) and no strays. The first short one is the first spawn after it, at 11:06:02.

**Rapt0r's side matches too.**
- The resync asks (rs|j crumbs): 3 before 11:03:33, then 62 in 18 waves from 11:06:20 to 12:02:22 (plus a wave of 3 at 12:05:09, after the run's end).
- The R30 run had no Alicorn spawn and only 8 rs answered.
- Rapt0r has 47 stray lines with 86 copies. The first is at 13:06:21, for ERA_Unit_02_Dep_Air1 #2-#4, which is the host's 1-of-4 flight.
- He has 53 "planes bound" lines. His strays are all "#ord" copies, none a BP_ name: #4 x27, #2 x19, #6 x14, #3 x13, #5 x8, #1 x5.
- His own pools never clashed: "SV_Unit_Alicorn here (a joiner's copies) NOT removed (204 alive)" at 13:03:12, so they were never freed during the run.

**Still open at HEAD.** `git diff 1717cef HEAD -- sv_alicorn.lua` is empty. sv_coop.lua :505 (hostPlane) and :1154 (clientPlane) still test the set with no unit check. No later build fixes it.

One caveat: addresses aren't logged, so the reuse itself is inferred. But it is the only path left in the code, and the timing fits.
verdicts.corrected_status: new, open at HEAD
verdicts.fix:
Check the set only for the Alicorn's own unit.
- sv_coop.lua:505 (hostPlane): `if unit == "SV_Unit_Alicorn" and SPC.alcnPool and a and SPC.alcnPool.set[a] then return end`
- sv_coop.lua:1154 (clientPlane): the same, as `if unit == "SV_Unit_Alicorn" and SPC and SPC.alcnPool and a and SPC.alcnPool.set[a] then return end`

This is safe because pool planes always arrive under that unit: SPC.alicornPooled returns early unless `unit == UNIT`.

- In 0.73.79 (commit 1717cef), sv_coop.lua hostPlane at :462-478 has only two early returns: no M.units entry, which would drop the whole flight rather than part of it, and `SPC.alcnPool.set[a]`.

- At HEAD it can also hit any later run in the same session, on the host until the next Alicorn and on a joiner for good: freed pool addresses reused after a restart or new level are skipped too.

verdicts.fix:
Skip the parked pools only for the Alicorn's own unit. SPC.alicornPooled admits only unit == UNIT, and SPC.alicornUnit is that constant (sv_alicorn.lua:10).

findings.title: Host tick 14 -> 58 -> 64 ms and fps ~37 -> ~24; SV_UnitAlive's cost per call tracks units spawned, and the round-8 Spaceport front-loaded it
findings.evidence:
All 23 perf windows, grouped by phase. Columns: tick avg (first half + second half); SV_UnitAlive calls a tick and ms a tick; distinct units spawned so far (native 'spawn X: up').
- r1-7: 14.2 (7.5+6.7); 1.4 calls / 1.8 ms; 3-17 units.
- r8 Spaceport window (10:24:38): 52.6 (36.3+16.3); 7.0 calls / 29.0 ms.
- r10-19: 58.3 (35.7+22.7); 4.4 / 28.8.
- r20-31: 63.5 (34.0+29.6); 5.0 / 35.2 ms, 55% of the tick.

Per call: 0.68 ms at 3 units (10:03:50), 1.85 at 17 (10:19:09), 4.14 at 49 (10:24:38), 6.00 at 57 (10:29:46), 6.4-7.4 at 65-88 (to 12:00:09). That fits about 75-80 us per unit.

Worst halves were 235-400 ms in every window from r8 ('rounds' 228-358), and 847 ms at 12:00:09 ('rounds' 819; VALKA's end / round 31's start).

The host's fps proxy ('frames fed' per minute) went 37-39 (r2-6), 31-33 (r7-10), 27-29 (r11-15), 22-25 (r16-31). The players' note: 'fps from around wave 22'.

The Lua heap stayed at 5.9-12.0 MB with no trend.

Against R30 (Spaceport at r21): R30's host was at 15.7 / 29.5 / 59.4 ms; this one reached the late-run level by round 11.
findings.cause: runtime/survival_rt.c:1517 UnitAlive -> RegisteredUnit (:1378), a linear scan of the phase unit list with Readable()/VirtualQuery (:221) per entry. Every unit spawned stays registered (see A4). This is unchanged at HEAD (runtime 0.32.24).
findings.fix: As R30: in the runtime, keep each desc's unit pointer from Spawn, check it with uobj.h UObjLive instead of the VirtualQuery scan, and cache FindDesc by FName. Until then, use the Lua mitigations A3 and A4.

verdicts.reason:
I confirmed this from the logs and the code. It is KNOWN (R30's root-cause finding) and still OPEN at HEAD.

Logs (a_31round/SaintAlessia-logs/AC8SurvivalMode_lua.log, the 23 `perf:` and `perf: lists:` pairs):
- All the phase averages are exact.
  - r1-7 (4 windows): tick 14.2 ms; SV_UnitAlive 1.43 calls and 1.83 ms a tick.
  - r8-19 (7 windows, 10:29:46 to 11:01:37): tick 58.3; 4.41 calls, 28.8 ms.
  - r20-31 (11 windows): tick 63.5; 35.2 ms, which is 55% of the tick.
- Cost per call against distinct units spawned (AC8SurvivalMode.log `spawn X: up`, recounted):
  - 10:03:50: 0.54/0.8 = 0.68 ms, 3 units.
  - 10:19:09: 3.14/1.7 = 1.85 ms, 17 units.
  - 10:24:38: 28.96/7.0 = 4.14 ms, 49 units.
  - 10:29:46: 13.79/2.3 = 6.0 ms, 57 units.
  - 12:00:09: 7.1 ms, 88 units.
  - The fit is about 0.6 ms + 75 us a unit. Only 3 units were taken off the list and never spawned again, so the list is about 85 long at the end.
- Round 8 was the Spaceport ("round 8, the Spaceport Assault: 27 ships", 10:19:41), which took the count from 17 to 49 units.
- The fps proxy (`frames fed` a minute): 37-39 in r2-6, about 30 by r10, 21-27 from r16.

It is units, not elapsed time, that drive the cost. At the same time after level start, d_alessia (0.73.81) had fewer units and a lower cost per call:
- About 22 min in: 1.69 ms (18 units) against 4.14 ms (49 units).
- About 42 min in: 2.86 ms (31 units) against 6.45 ms (69 units).
- d_alessia's slope, (2.86 - 0.66) / 29 units, is 76 us a unit, the same as a_31round's.

Two small corrections:
- The worst-half 'rounds' was 228-358 in every window from r8 except 11:38:51, where it was 49.
- Putting the 847 ms at "VALKA's end / round 31's start" is a guess: the window 11:54:48-12:00:09 holds both, at 11:58:02 and 11:58:19.

Code:
- The blamed lines are right: survival_rt.c:221 Readable (VirtualQuery), :1378 RegisteredUnit (a linear scan of the phase list with Readable on each entry, plus UnitId's second Readable on the vtable and a virtual call), :1517 UnitAlive.
- These functions are byte for byte the same at 294712f (runtime 0.32.23, which the log ran) and at HEAD (0.32.24).
- A unit leaves the phase list only through Recycle, that is, when the same desc spawns again.

Not fixed at HEAD:
- 0.73.80's Lua ALIVE cache (sv_spawn.lua:155-283, 8-32 asks a second) is only a mitigation. d_alessia is its first in-game run: 2.0-3.0 calls a tick at r11-14, against 4.2-4.6 at the same rounds here, so about 40% fewer calls.
- The cost per call still grows at about 76 us a unit. At 88 units, 2.5 asks a tick would still cost about 18 ms a tick, and a Spaceport round with many hulls watched (up to 32 asks a second) about 56 ms.

The finding's fix (keep each desc's unit pointer and check it with UObjLive, cache FindDesc) is right. The smallest version is below.
verdicts.fix:
The smallest fix is in runtime/survival_rt.c only; nothing in Lua changes.

1. RegisteredUnit (:1378): check each entry without VirtualQuery. Replace `Readable(u, LY.idIface + 8)` with `(UObjLive(u) == 1 || (UObjLive(u) < 0 && Readable(u, LY.idIface + 8)))`. uobj.h is already included at :25.

2. UnitId (:1370): replace `Readable(vt + LY.idSlot / 8, 8)` with `InGame(vt + LY.idSlot / 8)`. That is :243, the exe image range: AC8's vtables are in its image.

3. Put a small cache in front of the scan: a static array of {id, unit} pairs. On a lookup, return the cached unit when that exact pointer is still in PhaseUnits()->data (a plain pointer compare over at most 4096 entries, with no syscalls) and UObjLive(unit) == 1. Otherwise scan as above and store the result. Drop the cache in SV_Reset and in the teardown gate, and drop an id's entry in Recycle.

4. Optionally, cache FindDesc by the FName's index and number. The UnitDescList is fixed for a world data, so clear the cache when g_wd changes.

This makes UnitAlive's cost flat in the units spawned: each entry costs nanoseconds instead of two VirtualQuery calls (about 75 us). The base of about 0.6 ms a call comes from VirtualQuery in LiveObject, PhaseWorldData and ObjGoneWhy. It can be cut the same way later: LiveObject can use UObjLive when g_uoChunks is set.

To check it, run the same `perf: lists:` natives line. The ms per SV_UnitAlive call should stay under about 0.7 ms through round 30. Keep 0.73.80's ALIVE cache as it is.
verdicts.corrected_status: known-open (confirmed): the native cause is unchanged at HEAD (runtime 0.32.24). 0.73.80's Lua ALIVE cache cut the calls about 40% in its first in-game run (d_alessia), but the cost per call still grows about 76 us a unit.

verdicts.reason:
I checked the finding against the logs and the code and could not refute it. Each number below comes from a_31round/SaintAlessia-logs.

- **Tick times.** There are 23 perf windows. Phase averages: r1-7 is 14.2 ms (7.5+6.7), r8 is 52.6 (36.3+16.3), r9-19 (10:29:46-11:01:37) is 58.3 (35.7+22.7), and r20-31 (11 windows) is 63.5. The 'natives' part of the perf lines gives SV_UnitAlive per phase: 1.4 calls and 1.83 ms a tick, then 7.0 / 28.96, then 4.4 / 28.8, then 5.0 / 35.2. The last is 55% of the tick.
- **Cost per call against distinct units** (counted from 'spawn X: up' in AC8SurvivalMode.log): 0.68 ms at 3 units, 1.85 at 17, 4.14 at 49, 6.0 at 57, and 6.32-7.37 at 65-88. That is about 76 us per unit.
- **Round 8 front-loaded it.** The Spaceport registered 32 new SV_Unit_Sp* units in one round (14 Aegis, 8 boats, the Ford, 4 Wasps, 5 LCACs), taking distinct units from 17 to 49. None was ever recycled. The whole run has only 7 SV_Recycle calls (VoidWatcher x4, the Alicorn, 2 ERA flights).
- **A second session agrees.** The 0.73.81 run (d_alessia) shows the same slope on its own: 0.66 ms a call at 2 units, 2.86 ms at 31 units, about 76 us per unit.
- **fps proxy** (player 3's 'frames fed' / 60) averages 36.4 / 30.6 / 28.5 / 24.8 by phase. The claim said 37-39 / 31-33 / 27-29 / 22-25. The trend holds; r16-31 actually ranges 19.2-29.3.
- **R30 comparison** (15.7 / 29.5 / 59.4) matches R30_FINDINGS.json.
- **Lua heap** stays at 5.9-12.0 MB with no trend.

Small errors in the finding:
- 'rounds' was not the worst part in every window from r8. At 11:38:51 its worst was 49 ms, and that window's 250 ms worst half was the second half.
- The lowest late cost per call is 6.32 ms (at 10:34:59), not 6.4.

The cause holds at both the 0.73.79 build (1717cef) and HEAD:
- runtime/survival_rt.c:1517 UnitAlive calls RegisteredUnit (:1378). That is a linear scan of the phase list. For each entry it calls Readable(u) (one VirtualQuery, :221), then UnitId (:1370), which calls Readable on the vtable (a second VirtualQuery) and makes a virtual call.
- Spawn (:1467) and Recycle (:1400) use the same scan.
- Since 1717cef, runtime/ has changed only in 931f651 and fd228a5 (fwkind). The scan is unchanged at 0.32.24.

Status: KNOWN (R30 perf findings 1/2) and still OPEN at HEAD:
- **0.73.80's ALIVE cache helps only partly.** sv_spawn.lua:152-271 sets the ask rate by the number of units watched, from 8 to 32 a second. Late rounds with about 20 flights watched would still ask about 20 a second, the same rate as this run.
- **In the 0.73.81 run** it cut calls to 1.1-3.0 a tick (against 2.3-4.6 here at the same rounds), but did nothing about the cost per call.
- **Many callers at HEAD skip ALIVE** and call SV_UnitAlive directly: sv_allies.lua:680/702/763 (allies/counts was 13.7 ms a tick at 12:00:09), sv_shop.lua:185/232/243, sv_amphib.lua, sv_anomalies.lua, sv_rounds.lua:821 and sv_spaceport.lua:1343.

The fix the finding proposes would work. The smallest fix is below.

- Correct that nothing recycles the sunk fleet or the wave and lane units. At HEAD:

findings.title: The Alicorn's VLS are never matched in its spawn record, so every look walks every object (the 0.73.79 checklist line appeared)
findings.evidence:

The finding holds, but it overstates the cost.

**The log line.** I checked the host's AC8SurvivalMode_lua.log for a_31round.
- Line 6714 at 11:00:48 is the only "found by a search" line in the run: "the Alicorn's BP_BA002_alcn_vls_Base_C: 4 found by a search (not in its record)".
- UE4SS.log line 8392 puts it at 11:00:48.073. The core's health line came 81 ms earlier (47.992), and the 33-parts line follows at 48.086.
- Line 6717 says "VLS found: 4". The weapons log at lines 6755-6758 names the shooters vlsL1, vlsL2, vlsR1 and vlsR2.
- AGENTS.md's 0.73.79 checklist says this line should not appear.
- R30_FINDINGS.json does not mention it, so it is new. It is the only Alicorn round in this run. The 0.73.78 runs predate the spawn-record code.

**The cause.** The code is sv_alicorn.lua's parts(), lines 190-221. HEAD is identical to the 0.73.79 patch: `git diff 1717cef HEAD` on the file is empty, and it was last changed in bdbaeab.
- It builds `short = cls:gsub("_C$","").."_C_"` (line 203) and matches the spawn record by name (lines 205-206).
- `BP_BA002_alcn_vls_Base_C` is listed both in ARMS vls classes (line 254) and in CFG.specials.alicorn.weapon_classes (sv_config.lua:1484).
- That class has no instances of its own. ALICORN.md 1.1 has Hatch/BP_BA002_alcn_vls{L,R}{1,2}_Base as subclasses of Weapon/BP_BA002_alcn_vls_Base, and the Alicorn's parts 31-34 are those four.
- So no recorded object's name matches the base class's prefix, and FindAllOf walks. FindAllOf also returns subclass instances, which is how it found the same 4 objects. armsLook removed the duplicates by address, so "VLS found: 4", not 8.
- The four subclass entries did match their record: none of them logged a search.
- The line appeared before "33 parts lowered", so the walk came from the weapons-scaling loop (pairs over weapon_classes), not from armsUp.

**What is overstated.** The finding says every call with an empty list, and every fresh look, falls back to FindAllOf.
- After that first walk, the class's cached list holds the 4 objects. Dead entries stay in the list, so it never counts as empty again and non-fresh calls never walk again.
- The fresh look-again walks every class in the kind whatever the record holds (`if fresh or ...`), by design since bdbaeab. It ran once for the VLS, when they went down at 11:02:45.
- The real waste per Alicorn fight is one walk of about 40 ms at its first weapons check. The fresh look at VLS-down also makes a fifth, redundant walk.
- "Minor" is the right severity. The status is NEW and still open at HEAD, unchanged in 0.73.80, 0.73.81 and 0.73.82.
verdicts.corrected_status: new (open at HEAD; costs one FindAllOf, about 40 ms, per Alicorn fight plus one redundant walk in the VLS-down fresh look, not one on every call)
verdicts.fix:
Remove "BP_BA002_alcn_vls_Base_C" from two lists:

The record now covers every listed class, so no first-check walk happens and the VLS-down fresh look makes 4 walks, not 5.

Two alternatives are worse:
- Matching the record by the prefix "BP_BA002_alcn_vls" for the base class would only duplicate the subclass entries.

The only entry that misses the record is the fifth one, the base class BP_BA002_alcn_vls_Base_C. Its instances are all subclasses, so a name prefix can't match them. Its FindAllOf found the same 4 parts: armsLook de-duplicates by address and reported "the Alicorn's VLS found: 4" (line 6717), not 8.

findings.title: The pay audit (TESTER logger) logs co-op special pays before the split, about doubling 'specials'
findings.evidence:
- 10:41:24 (line 4425): 'specials 1 (+11900)', while the pay was 'credits: +5950 (MINDRIPPER down, co-op share x0.50 of 11900 (4 players))'.
- 11:58:03 (12930): 'specials 1 (+18000)' for 'credits: +8050 (VALKA down, co-op share x0.45 of 18000 (5 players))'.
- Over the run the audit summed specials at 168,720 Z (60 pays) against 82,576 actually paid; its total of +430,400 overstates the host's income.
- The kills audit was right: 145,430 audited against 145,730 paid.
findings.cause: sv_audit.lua:131-137 wraps the global addCredits after sv_coop.lua:5147 has wrapped it. The split happens inside sv_coop's wrapper, so AUDIT.pay sees the caller's whole amount.
findings.fix: Audit the amount actually paid. For example, let sv_coop expose a hook that wraps its inner rawAddCredits, and have sv_audit wrap that one instead of the outer addCredits.

verdicts.reason:
I confirmed this from the logs and the code, at the build the log ran and at HEAD.

Logs: a_31round/SaintAlessia-logs/AC8SurvivalMode_lua.log.
- The two examples hold:
  - Line 4320, 10:40:37: "credits: +5950 (MINDRIPPER down, co-op share x0.50 of 11900 (4 players))". The audit at line 4425, 10:41:24, says "specials 1 (+11900)".
  - Line 12909, 11:58:02: "credits: +8050 (VALKA down, co-op share x0.45 of 18000 (5 players))". The audit at line 12930, 11:58:03, says "specials 1 (+18000)".
- Run totals: the 115 audit lines add up to +430,400. By kind: kills 863 pays (+145,430), round bonuses 30 (+116,250), specials 60 (+168,720).
- I put the 955 "credits:" lines through the audit's own kindOf rules, counting only pays up to the last audit line (13517).
  - Kills: 863 pays, +145,430, an exact match.
  - Round bonuses: 30 pays, +116,250, an exact match.
  - Specials: 60 pays, +82,576 actually paid. All 60 are "co-op share" pays, and their whole amounts add up to exactly 168,720.
  - So the audit counts specials at about 2.04x what was paid, and its total overstates the host's income by 86,144 Z.
  - The analyst's 145,730 for kills paid includes one +300 kill at 12:04:37, after the last audit line. That is a small slip and doesn't change the finding.
- The same thing happens on 0.73.81 (d_alessia host log):
  - Line 1604: "AB.L..IN down, co-op share x0.58 of 8750" (+5052 paid). The audit at line 1676 says "specials 1 (+8750)".
  - Lines 2023 and 2047: two Ladons at +4503 each. The audit at line 2067 says "specials 2 (+15600)".

Code:
- main.lua's MODULES list loads sv_coop (line 34) before sv_audit (line 36).
- sv_coop.lua keeps sv_ai's function as a local (`local rawAddCredits = addCredits`: line 4188 at 1717cef, the 0.73.79 patch; line 5264 at HEAD in the working tree). It then replaces the global addCredits with a wrapper. That wrapper changes n to specialPay(whole) and adds "co-op share" to why, then calls rawAddCredits(n, why).
- sv_audit.lua lines 131-137 (the same at 1717cef, 36c2b03 and HEAD 7829f66) then wrap the global again. AUDIT.pay(n, why) therefore runs before the split and sees the caller's whole amount.
- On a joiner, the "cr" handler calls the global addCredits with the share already taken, so joiners' audits are right. A side effect: a round bonus that M.noDownBonus holds back is still counted by the host's audit.
- Nothing after the build fixes it. The last commit to touch sv_audit.lua is 4cf20c4 (0.73.78), and the uncommitted changes don't touch the pay path.

The status "new" is right. The audit is a TESTER/dev-only logger (friends' zips have it off), so "minor" fits.
verdicts.fix:
Audit the pay itself, after sv_coop's split, through a hook that sv_coop exposes.

1. In sv_coop.lua (HEAD line ~5264), keep the inner function on COOP:

```lua
local rawAddCredits = addCredits
COOP.payInner = rawAddCredits      -- the pay itself, after the co-op split (sv_audit wraps this)
```

2. In the same file's wrapper, change the paying call from `rawAddCredits(n, why)` to `COOP.payInner(n, why)`.

3. In sv_audit.lua lines 131-137, wrap that hook when it's there, and fall back to the global otherwise:

```lua
do
    local onCoop = COOP and type(COOP.payInner) == "function"
    local rawAdd = onCoop and COOP.payInner or addCredits
    if type(rawAdd) == "function" then
        local w = function(n, why) pcall(AUDIT.pay, n, why); return rawAdd(n, why) end
        if onCoop then COOP.payInner = w else addCredits = w end
    end
end
```

Why this covers every case:
- Every pay still passes through sv_coop's wrapper, then its inner call: solo, the host and a joiner's "cr" pays alike. So the audit sees each amount as paid.
- A round bonus held back while you're DOWN is no longer counted.
- audit_test.lua, which stubs only addCredits and has no COOP.payInner, keeps working through the fallback.

Add one case to audit_test: a COOP stub with payInner and a 0.5 share. A special of 11900 should be audited as +5950.

verdicts.reason:

Code:

verdicts.corrected_status: new, still open at HEAD (sv_audit.lua unchanged since 0.73.79; also seen in the 0.73.81 run)
verdicts.fix:
Smallest fix, in sv_audit.lua only: audit what was actually added to RUN.earned, not the amount asked for. In sv_audit.lua:130-138, replace the wrapper with:

    addCredits = function(n, why)
        local before = RUN and RUN.earned or 0
        local r = rawAdd(n, why)
        local paid = (RUN and RUN.earned or 0) - before
        if paid ~= 0 then pcall(AUDIT.pay, paid, why) end
        return r
    end

This logs the post-split share. It also skips a round bonus that M.noDownBonus held back, and includes the SETUP.payX income multiplier. kindOf still sorts by the caller's why, so the categories stay the same.

Equivalent alternative: call pcall(AUDIT.pay, n, why) inside sv_ai.lua's addCredits after payX (when AUDIT exists) and drop the wrapper.

Add a check to audit_test: a host with 4 players gets addCredits(11900, "MINDRIPPER down"), and the audit must log specials +5950.

findings.title: The host-migration line is re-sent and logged every few seconds as round-trip jitter reorders joiners with near-equal scores
findings.evidence: 719 'coop: migration: the next hosts, best link first' lines in 2 h, about 5.9 a minute, e.g. '4 (102), 2 (116), 5 (120), 3 (122)' then '4 (96), 5 (110), 2 (116), 3 (118)' 10 s later. The scores sit within 96-128. Each logged change is also a reliable 'sq' to every joiner.
findings.cause: sv_coop.lua:4395-4421 re-ranks every 5 s on the raw rtt (+2000 x loss) and sends and logs whenever the order string changes.
findings.fix: Add hysteresis. Keep the current order unless a joiner beats the one above it by more than about 30 ms (or bucket the score to 50 ms), and log the line at most once a minute.

verdicts.reason:
The finding is confirmed from the logs and from the code at both builds. One correction: the line numbers it gives are wrong.

Logs, a_31round host, AC8SurvivalMode_lua.log (UE4SS.log has the same 719):
- 719 "coop: migration: the next hosts, best link first" lines. The first is at 10:02:36 and the last at 12:04:56: 122.3 min, so 5.88 a minute. That is 5.3% of the log's 13,623 lines.
- The quoted pair is real: 12:04:45 "4 (102), 2 (116), 5 (120), 3 (122)", then 12:04:56 "4 (96), 5 (110), 2 (116), 3 (118)".
- Of the 718 changes between lines, 710 are pure reorders: the same players, and nobody crossing the +10000 "not fresh" penalty. Only 6 changed who was in the list and 2 changed the penalty. The first in line changed 364 times.
- In those reorders, 1,016 pairs of players swapped places. The score gap after a swap has a median of 7 ms, 923 are 20 ms or less and 985 (97%) are 30 ms or less.
- Scores while in the mission run 89 to 753, with a median of 119 and a 95th percentile of 145, so "96-128" is about right.
- 403 of the gaps between lines are exactly 5 s, which is the 5-s re-rank.
- The 0.73.81 run (d_alessia) shows the same thing at a lower rate: 69 lines in 37.3 min (1.85 a minute), 57 of them pure reorders, 56 of 57 swaps within 30 ms.
- No migration happened in either run. Rapt0r's log has no migration line, so the cost seen is log spam and extra reliable broadcasts. A host drop would also be more likely to leave the joiners holding different lines; migStepBack covers that case.

Code: hostShare in sv_coop.lua.
- At HEAD it is at lines 4511-4540, not 4395-4421. In the 0.73.79 TESTER patch's file (commit 1717cef) it is at about 3460-3486.
- The function is identical in the two builds (diff: same). It has been unchanged since bbb6fce (0.73.30), so no later build fixes it.
- `M.sqAt = now + 5` re-ranks every 5 s. The score is raw rtt, + 2000 x the share resent, + 10000 when the player isn't fresh, with slot as the tie-break.
- `if order ~= M.sqSent ... then send(true, "sq", me, order)` sends whenever the order string changes, and also every 30 s.
- `if order ~= M.sqSaid then log(...)` logs on the same order string, so every logged line is also an "sq" sent.
- send(true, ...) is sendTo(nil, reliable), which reaches SV_CoopSend(..., 1, -1): a reliable message to every other game.

Status: new, still open at HEAD (7829f66), minor.
verdicts.corrected_status: new (open at HEAD; cause is sv_coop.lua hostShare at lines 4511-4540 at HEAD, about 3460-3486 in 0.73.79's file, not 4395-4421)
verdicts.fix:
Add hysteresis in sv_coop.lua hostShare (HEAD lines 4511-4540). Keep the existing table.sort as it is. Right after it, put back any adjacent pair whose earlier order the new scores don't beat by more than a margin. Don't put the margin in the sort's comparator: that makes the comparator inconsistent and Lua's table.sort can fail with "invalid order function". After the sort:

    local HYST = (mig().rank_hyst_ms or 30)
    local prev = {}
    for i, s in ipairs(M.sqRank or {}) do prev[s] = i end
    for _ = 1, #list do
        for i = 1, #list - 1 do
            local a, b = list[i], list[i + 1]
            if prev[a.s] and prev[b.s] and prev[b.s] < prev[a.s] and b.score - a.score <= HYST then
                list[i], list[i + 1] = b, a
            end
        end
    end
    M.sqRank = {}
    for i, e in ipairs(list) do M.sqRank[i] = e.s end

Clear M.sqRank wherever the role or the host changes (a takeover, opening as host), so a new host doesn't inherit an old ranking.

Effect: the +10000 not-fresh penalty and real loss (2000 x the share resent) still reorder the line at once. In this log 97% of the swaps were within 30 ms, so the sends and log lines should drop from about 5.9 a minute to well under 1. The 30-s refresh send stays as it is.

Optionally, write the log line only when the first in line changes or 60 s have passed, while still sending on every change. Add a case to tools/checks/coop_migration_test.sh: scores 102/116/120/122 followed by 96/110/116/118 must give no new "sq" and no new log line.

verdicts.reason:
Confirmed from the log and the code. The cause and the fix hold. Only the line numbers have moved.

Log, a_31round/SaintAlessia-logs/AC8SurvivalMode_lua.log:
- There are exactly 719 lines of 'coop: migration: the next hosts, best link first'. The first is at 10:02:36 (line 367) and the last at 12:04:56, so 122.3 min and 5.88 a minute.
- The rate grows through the run: 2-8 a minute until about 11:30, then 7-12 a minute from 11:36 to 12:04. hostShare runs at most every 5 s, so 12 a minute is a change on every check.
- Both quoted examples are real. 12:04:45 has '4 (102), 2 (116), 5 (120), 3 (122)' and 12:04:56 has '4 (96), 5 (110), 2 (116), 3 (118)', 11 s apart.
- I sorted each of the 718 changes by type with a script (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-ac8survivalmod/a8f161c4-52df-54fa-bd8c-2e7169d4b274/scratchpad/mig.py):
  - 6 are a player joining or leaving.
  - 2 are a player moving into or out of the +10000 not-fresh penalty.
  - 710 are pure reorders of the same players. In 679 of those (95.6%) every pair that swapped places was less than 30 apart in score; in 705 (99.3%) less than 50.
- Without the penalty, scores run from 89 to 753; the 5th to 95th percentile is 98 to 144 and the median is 118. The claim's '96-128' is right for the late-run lines.
- The same thing shows in d_alessia's 0.73.81 host log: 69 lines from 12:44:27 to 13:21:45 (about 1.9 a minute with fewer players). 56 of its 57 pure reorders have swapped pairs less than 30 apart.

Code: hostShare (sv_coop.lua) runs every 5 s (M.sqAt = now + 5).
- It scores each player as rtt + 2000 x the share resent, plus 10000 when the player isn't fresh, then sorts on the raw score.
- When the order string changes, or every 30 s, it calls send(true, "sq", me, order). That is sendTo(nil, ...), a reliable message to every joiner.
- It logs whenever the order differs from M.sqSaid. So every reorder is both a log line and a reliable 'sq' broadcast.
- The function is identical at 294712f (0.73.79, line 3373) and at HEAD (line 4511); I diffed them. The finding's 4395-4421 is the 0.73.81/0.73.82 numbering (line 4394).
- No later build touches it, so it is still open at HEAD.

The impact is minor: noise in the log and about 6 reliable messages a minute to each joiner. The order is only used once the host has been silent for after_s 30, and choosing between links a few ms apart makes no difference.
verdicts.corrected_status: new (open at HEAD; the cause is at sv_coop.lua:4511-4541 at HEAD, 4394-4421 in 0.73.81/0.73.82, 3373 in 0.73.79)
verdicts.fix:
In hostShare, after the table.sort, keep the line already sent unless a change is real. Leave the sort itself alone: a hysteresis comparator isn't transitive, and Lua's table.sort can fail with one ('invalid order function').

1. Keep M.sqPos (slot -> position in the last order sent) and M.sqScore (slot -> its score then).
2. Treat the new order as a change only if one of these holds:
   - the set of slots changed;
   - a player crossed the 10000 not-fresh penalty;
   - in some pair that swapped places, the score gap is 30 or more (CFG.coop.migration.hysteresis, default 30).
3. If it isn't a change, set `order` back to M.sqSent before the `order ~= M.sqSent` test, so only the 30-s resend goes out.
4. Rate-limit the log line separately: say it when the first in line changes, otherwise at most once every 60 s (M.sqSaidAt).

With a margin of 30 this would have dropped 679 of the 718 changes in the 31-round log, and 56 of 57 in the 0.73.81 log, while players joining or leaving and real link changes still go out at once.

findings.title: Joiners' loadouts flicker: 144 'loadout changed' lines, each a hi resend; 14 of 1,210 replayed launches dropped
findings.evidence:
'coop: player N's loadout changed: their real plane here keeps the one it was spawned with':
- Aquila (player 5): 89 lines, 68 of them while his gear was down at the airfield; 58 between 11:32:38 and 11:33:59 (line 9766 on), 1-2 a second.
- OdyDio (player 3): 51 lines, 48 in flight.
- Rapt0r: 4.
Native T4b totals: 1,210 queued, 1,196 launched, 14 'not a weapon of their plane here', e.g. 'player 3's shot (weapon 3) NOT replayed ... it has 3 weapons' (10:24:18, 4x at 11:02:39).
findings.cause: R30's finding, still open. On a joiner, M.myLoadout() flips between values. HEAD sv_coop.lua:5663-5670 sends 'hi' on every change with no debounce, and :2643 logs every flip. In-flight flips (OdyDio) point at the special-weapon selection; the airfield ones at the hangar weapon pages (inference).
findings.fix: Send a changed loadout only after it has held about 3 s, and drop the selected-special field from the compared string. Log one 'loadout changed' line a level per player.

verdicts.reason:
The counts hold, but the cause is wrong, the in-flight evidence comes from a logging cap, and the proposed fix would break things.

Counts I re-checked (a_31round host, AC8SurvivalMode_lua.log):
- 144 'loadout changed' lines: player 5 89, player 3 51, player 4 4.
- Player 5 had 58 of them between 11:32:38 and 11:33:59 (line 9766 on), and 68 fall inside his two logged gear-down windows (11:32:13-11:33:50 and 11:38:01-11:39:25).
- The native T4b totals add up to 1,210 queued, 1,196 launched and 14 'not a weapon of their plane here'. There are 6 per-shot lines, all player 3's weapon 3.

1. This is not a flicker. The loadout really changes while the player is on the ground at the airfield, picking specials in the in-game hangar:
   - Rapt0r's own joiner log (b_Logs, about 2 h ahead of the host's clock) shows this at each of his 4 changes.
   - Host 10:26:24 = joiner 12:26:21-23: 'music: track clock held (landing store)', then 'shop: ammo panel WBP_Menu_IngameHangar_WeaponDetail_002 ... WBP_Menu_IngameHangar_Weapon1_000'.
   - Host 11:29:34 = joiner 13:29:32-34: 'weapon bays tier 2: special 1 full load 14 -> 28 (stock 14)' and one second later '8 -> 16 (stock 8)'. A different special was fitted.
   - In the 0.73.81 run (d_alessia, same code), every change line that falls where a gear flip was logged is inside a gear-down window. Examples: player 3 down 12:50:34, changes 12:50:57-12:51:03, up 12:51:36; player 4 down 13:18:01, changes 13:18:22-25, up 13:21:39.

2. The '48 of OdyDio's in flight' figure is an artifact. peersTick logs only a plane's first 4 gear flips (sv_coop.lua: 0.73.79 line 2729, HEAD line 3781, `if P.gearFlips <= 4`). Player 3's last logged flip is 10:11:44, so after that the analyst counted everything as in flight. In fact:
   - 32 of his 51 lines fall within 2 minutes of 'target (player 3) is landed at their airfield', one of his STORE builds or his gear going down.
   - 5 more fall in round breaks.
   - Only about 14 lines have no evidence either way, and none of them is shown to be in flight.
   - Aquila's other 21 lines are at 11:46:14-22 (14 s after round 27 cleared) and 12:04:25-31. Those also come after his gear-log cap.

3. The log does not fire on 'every flip'. The condition (0.73.79 line 2030, HEAD about 2777) is `lo ~= P.lo and P.loSaid ~= lo`. A change back to the spawn loadout, or a repeat of the last value logged, is not logged.

4. The 14 dropped shots come from a real change, not a flicker. Player 3's real plane spawned at 10:03:17 with special bytes '13,0' and has 3 weapons. His weapon 3 is a second special he fitted later (his first change was at 10:07:03, the first drop at 10:24:18). The whole run was one level, so the plane kept its spawn loadout, as designed since 0.73.12. A debounce would not change that.
   - This is R30's known finding. 0.73.80's weapon stand-ins (M.weaponFor / M.standInPay) are built for exactly this case.
   - They stay inactive until runtime 0.32.24 ships SV_PPWeapons. Without it M.ppKinds returns nil and the shot goes as sent.
   - The 0.73.81 run had 0 such drops (525 queued, 509 launched).

5. The proposed fix would cause harm. The trailing 'x,y' are the two fitted specials (+0xFA0/+0xFA1, tools/re/COOP2MP.md), not a 'selected special' field.
   - At HEAD, M.standInPay reads them (`M.loIds(r0.lo)` vs `M.loIds(P.lo)`, about line 3605) to find a changed special at its new number.
   - The next level's real plane spawns from r0.lo.
   - The rejoin check (about line 2708) compares lo too.
   - If they were left out of the comparison, a real special change at the airfield would never be sent.

6. The cited HEAD lines are stale. At HEAD the send is around 5787-5795 and the log around 2757-2777.

What is left at HEAD is cosmetic: the joiner sends one reliable 'hi' per selection while browsing specials at the airfield (144 in 2 h, at most 1-2 a second in bursts), and the host writes one line per change.
verdicts.corrected_status: WORKS-AS-INTENDED: players choosing specials in the in-game hangar at the airfield; the real plane keeps its spawn loadout by design. The 14 dropped replays are KNOWN (R30) and covered by 0.73.80's weapon stand-ins, which stay inactive until runtime 0.32.24 ships SV_PPWeapons. Only log and 'hi' noise remains open at HEAD, minor and cosmetic.
verdicts.fix:
Keep the special-weapon bytes in the compared string; dropping them would break the stand-in mapping and the next level's spawn. Optional noise cuts:
(1) In the joiner's send check (HEAD sv_coop.lua about 5787-5795), send a changed loadout only once it has held for 2 s. Set M.loPend and M.loPendAt when lo first differs from M.myLo. When os.clock() - M.loPendAt >= 2 and lo == M.loPend, call sendHi or hostRosterSelf. Row, code, paint and name changes still go at once.
(2) In peerTick (about 2777), log once per burst with both strings, which also settles which field moves: `coop: player N's loadout changed: <P.loSaid or P.lo> -> <lo> ...`, rate-limited to one line per slot every 10 s with a count of the changes in between.
The 14 drops need nothing new in Lua. Ship runtime 0.32.24 so the 0.73.80 stand-ins (SV_PPWeapons) can map a newly fitted special.

verdicts.reason:
The counts hold, but the finding misreads what happened. The cause it gives (an in-flight "flicker") is wrong, and half of the fix it proposes would break 0.73.80's weapon stand-ins.

What holds (a_31round host, AC8SurvivalMode_lua.log):
- There are 144 "loadout changed" lines: player 5 (Aquila) 89, player 3 (OdyDio) 51, player 4 (Rapt0r) 4.
- 58 of them fall between 11:32:38 and 11:33:59 (line 9766 on), all Aquila's.
- The native minute lines add up to 1,210 queued, 1,196 launched and 14 "not a weapon of their plane here". All 6 per-shot lines are player 3's weapon 3 against "it has 3 weapons" (10:24:18, 10:24:31, 4x at 11:02:39).
- The code is the same at the run's build (1717cef, sv_coop.lua:2030) and at HEAD (8068e5c: the log at :2757, the send at :5787-5797). The finding's :2643 and :5663 are 0.73.82's (21f8d41) line numbers. Each new value sends one "hi". The host then sends a "pi" for every roster slot to every joiner (hostRosterSelf -> sendRoster(nil), :547-557), with no throttle.

What is wrong:
1. The "in flight" counts (OdyDio 48 of 51, Aquila 21) are an artefact. The host logs a player's gear only for their first 4 flips (peersTick, `P.gearFlips <= 4`, sv_coop.lua:3781). Player 3's last gear line is at 10:11:44 and player 5's at 11:39:25, so every later change was counted as "in flight". The native once-a-minute lines ("fed from their stream: speed N m/s ... State X", State bit 9 = gear down) tell a different story:
   - Every change comes in a burst at an airfield stop.
   - OdyDio has about 20 bursts. Each sits next to a 0 m/s / State 27200 sample or a gear-down approach (e.g. 10:13:55-10:14:16 by 10:13:51 0 m/s 27200; 11:23:55-11:24:09, 11 lines, by 11:23:53 0 m/s).
   - Aquila's 89 come in 4 stops (11:32-11:33, 11:38, 11:46, 12:04), each with a 0 m/s State 27200 sample (11:32:54, 11:38:54, 11:46:54, 12:04:55).
2. It is not a flicker. These are real changes made by players browsing the landing menu's special-weapon pages (HangarWeaponSetting1/2). COOP2MP.md:434 saw the same thing on 2026-10-30. The changes depend on the player: Rapt0r has 16 stopped (0 m/s) samples but only 4 changes. In SV_CoopLoadout's "parts//x,y" string, the two bytes are the two equipped specials, 1 and 2 (+0xFA0 / +0xFA1, COOP2MP.md:502). They are not a "selected special".
3. The fix's "drop the selected-special field from the compared string" would break the 0.73.80 weapon stand-ins. Their case (b) (M.weaponFor, sv_coop.lua:3542-3551) reads ids.sh, the player's specials as they are now, which come from that field.
4. There is no measurable cost on the link. During Aquila's burst, the data sent to each joiner per minute stayed at 355-407 KB (before: 377 KB, during: 407 KB, after: 395 KB), the resend counts stayed flat (dukka 9, OdyDio 62, Rapt0r 46, Aquila 189) and the round trips stayed between 94 and 150 ms. The real cost is the log lines and a little reliable traffic.
5. The 14 drops are a consequence of a design choice, not of any flicker. A real plane is never spawned again mid-level, and a Survival run is one level: the host spawned only 3 real planes in 2 h (lines 435, 689, 9484). OdyDio's plane was spawned at 10:03:17 with "//13,0", so it has weapons 0-2. After his changes at the airfield he fired weapon 3. HEAD's weapon stand-ins already cover this case, but they need runtime 0.32.24's SV_PPWeapons. Without it, sv_coop.lua:3473 returns nil and the launches go as sent, and the 0.73.80-0.73.82 patches run on 0.32.23. So the drops are known, fixed at HEAD, and inactive until a full build ships runtime 0.32.24.
verdicts.corrected_status: The resends and log lines: known-open at HEAD, cosmetic or minor. Players changing specials at the airfield is intended. Each new value they browse to sends an unthrottled "hi" plus a "pi" for every roster slot to every joiner, and logs one line. The 14 dropped launches: known, fixed at HEAD by 0.73.80's weapon stand-ins, but inactive until a full build ships runtime 0.32.24 (the 0.73.80-0.73.82 patches run on 0.32.23).
verdicts.fix:
Smallest change at HEAD, keeping the special bytes in the loadout, because the stand-ins need them:

(1) In COOP.tick (sv_coop.lua:5787-5797), let a changed loadout through only once the same value has held for 2 s. Keep a pending value and its time (M.loPend / M.loPendAt). Compare `lo ~= "" and lo ~= M.myLo and M.loPend == lo and os.clock() - M.loPendAt >= 2` before calling sendHi / hostRosterSelf. The other fields (row, code, paint, aircraft name, class) still send at once.

(2) In peerTick (sv_coop.lua:2756), log one line per airfield stop: say it only when `not P.onAirfield` and lo ~= P.loSaid. Name the old and new specials, i.e. the trailing "x,y" of P.lo and of lo, so the next log shows what changed.

To stop the 14 drops, ship a full build on runtime 0.32.24; no Lua change is needed.

findings.title: VOID WATCHER's ESM field list only grows (3 -> 65 fields) and is walked every tick
findings.evidence: The perf lists' 'ESM fields' count went 3 (10:34) -> 11 -> 21 -> 31 -> 41 -> 50 -> 61 -> 65 (12:00) over 4 VOID WATCHER purchases. 'allies/VOID WATCHER' rose roughly linearly with it: 0.2 -> 0.6 -> 0.9 -> 1.1 -> 1.4 -> 1.5 -> 1.7 -> 2.0 ms a tick.
findings.cause: sv_allies.lua:1151-1168 loops over every field kept in R.esmFields each tick: liveAddr, nameOf and two property reads per field. A field is dropped only when its object is gone, and pooled fields from earlier VOID WATCHERs stay live.
findings.fix: Walk the fields only while a VOID WATCHER is airborne and only every 0.5 s. Drop fields not shown for 60 s, or those of a VOID WATCHER that went home.

verdicts.reason:
Confirmed from the logs and the code. The cause is right, and the loop is the same at HEAD as in the build the log ran.

Logs, a_31round host AC8SurvivalMode_lua.log, from the "perf: lists" and "perf: tick" lines:
- ESM fields go 3 (10:34:59), 11 (10:40:11, then flat through 10:56:16), 17, 21, 22, 23, 31, 41, 50 (11:33:39, then flat through 11:44:12), 54, 61, 65 (12:00:09).
- allies/VOID WATCHER goes 0.2, 0.6, 0.7, 0.3, 0.3, 0.7, 0.9, 0.8, 0.7, 1.1, 1.4, 1.5, 1.3, 1.3, 1.5, 1.7, 2.0 ms a tick over the same lines.
- There were 4 purchases (10:32:19, 10:57:45, 11:15:27, 11:47:09), each sent home and recycled (10:44:05, 11:10:20, 11:35:21, 12:00:23).

The cost doesn't depend on a VOID WATCHER being up:
- With none up it is still 0.3 ms at 11 fields (10:50:38, 10:56:16) and 1.3 ms at 50 fields (11:38:51, 11:44:12). That is about 26-27 us per field per tick, so the cost is linear in the list.
- The solo c_casual44 run (0.73.78) shows the same: 7 purchases, ESM fields 10 -> 181, the share 0.3 -> 2.1 ms. It was still 2.1 ms at 180 fields at 03:59:25, when none was up (sent home 03:50:10, the next bought 04:03:03).
- The count never goes down in either run, so the old fields stay in GUObjectArray. They also pass liveAddr and the name check.

New detail: the walk never did anything useful in these runs.
- There are 0 "launched again" lines in both logs. esmSet logs the first two "again" sets, so the again-branch (sv_allies.lua:1165) never ran in 11 VOID WATCHER lifetimes.
- The list grows by about one field per ESM fire (every 30 s): VOID WATCHER 3 went 22 -> 50 in about 17 minutes, the casual run 8 per 5 minutes. So each launch builds a new BP_wp_esm_MS28_C, and the 0.73.73 premise that these fields are reused from a pool doesn't hold here.

Code:

findings.cause: By design: the host's leaderboard line is the run's count less the joiners'. The sync tally comes from hostKiller (damage, or the host fired within 15 s), and a beam doesn't show as fired.
findings.fix: Optional: count the player's own LiveAttachedInstantWeapon or beam damage as 'fired' in hostKiller, so the sync tally and the joiners' attribution don't drop beam kills.

analysts.summary:
Rapt0r was player 4, a joiner on the 0.73.79 players' patch. His clock runs 1:59:59 ahead of the host's: round 31 cleared at 14:04:35 on his game and 12:04:36 on the host's. Survival's own accounting was correct for him. All 117 of his kills reached the host and matched its player-4 kills within ±2 s. He was paid x1 for them and x0.33 / x0.25 for 640 teammates' kills, and the host's tally and leaderboard list him at 117 air / 6 ground. His three complaints have these causes.

(1) "Score" is the game's own SCORE row, which Survival keeps on screen. On a joiner it never counts a kill: every copy is held at the 1 HP floor, and the host's "dn" takes it down with the host's AI F-16C stand-in as the cause. The host flies a Falken, which has no player blueprint on joiners. The only enemies he could kill the game's own way were the round-23 LCACs, which got no co-op ids in 0.73.79. Separately, the mirrored 'ROUND N KILLS / YOU N' callout showed him the host's kill counts, wrong in 8 of 9 rounds.

(2) He saw only HIT, never DESTROYED, for the same floor and cause reason. HEAD's M.dnKill uses his plane as the cause when the host names him, which per the RE notes should restore the game's DESTROYED and kill score, but nobody has seen it in game yet. kill_callout is off by default, and the host still names the player with the most damage, not the final blow.

(3) The late stutter. The host's frame rate fell from 35 to 25 fps as its Lua tick grew from 23 to 64 ms; SV_UnitAlive alone took 27-41 ms a tick from round 9. Enemy moves past their newest state rose from 2.8% to about 5%. Rapt0r's own frame rate stayed flat at about 76 fps.

NEW and open at HEAD: the step at round 20 (the 'desync' both Rapt0r and the host noted) starts right after the Alicorn round. SPC.alcnPool keeps the 131 parked-pool addresses after the Alicorn is gone. Once the host freed those planes (11:04:03), hostPlane skipped new enemy planes that reused those addresses. Before that, 0 of 171 flights were partially bound; after it, 53 of 110 were. That meant 17 resyncs, 86 stray copies and 83 enemy planes the joiners never got. The host answered 3 resync asks in the hour before and 62 in the hour after, three joiners at a time.

Also open at HEAD:
- allies/counts asks SV_UnitAlive directly (sv_allies.lua is unchanged since 0.73.79): 13 ms a tick on the host and 6.2 on the joiner late in the run.
- The leave probe costs the joiner 3 ms a tick.
- Every VOID WATCHER removal (4 of 4) caused a held burst and left a ghost copy for 6-14 minutes.
- The native minute line goes negative after a rebind.

Fixed later:
- The landing-window walks at the airfield (up to 25 ms a tick on Rapt0r; 0.73.80's LANDW cut them to 6-23 walks per 5 minutes on the 0.73.81 host).
- The LCAC co-op ids.
- The SV_UnitAlive asks of rounds, orders, Wolf holds, the shuttle and the Spaceport (0.73.80's ALIVE cache).

findings.title: From round 20, the host stops giving co-op ids to some new enemy planes: a stale Alicorn pool address set (this is the 'desync')
findings.evidence:
Rapt0r AC8SurvivalMode_lua.log, 12:08-13:06 (rounds 2-19): 0 partial binds, 0 strays, 0 resyncs after his join. From 13:06:21 to 14:02:24: 17 jn/rs resyncs and 47 stray takedowns (86 copies). 53 of 110 aircraft flights were partially bound, leaving 83 planes with no host id.

Bound-line examples:
- l.4393 '13:06:31 coop: the host's ERA_Unit_07_Dep_Air0 here: 0 of 2 planes bound ... (spawned as gen 237; the host's last ids for it: 2 for gen 224)'.
- l.4534 '13:08:44 ... ERA_Unit_04_Dep_Air1 here: 3 of 4 ... 6 for gen 243'. hostSync resends every 'bd' (0.73.79 sv_coop.lua:765), so 6 = 3 + 3 resent by the 13:08:34 repair: the host only ever had 3 ids. The host created all 4 planes (host lua l.7438-7441, 11:08:22).
- The pattern holds throughout: '2 of 4 / 4 ids', '5 of 6 / 10 ids'.

Timing:
- Host l.6719 '11:00:50 special: the Alicorn's pooled aircraft: 131 put away'.
- Host crumbs l.867-868 '11:04:03.850 recycle SV_Unit_Alicorn: destroying its old unit actor ... destroyed'.
- Gens 226-233, spawned 13:03:35-58 joiner time (before the destroy), bound fully. The first flights after it (gens 234+, from 13:05:58) are the first affected.

Host side:
- The sync lines show 3 resync asks answered in the 59 min before 11:04 and 62 in the 59 min after, in waves of 3, every joiner at once (l.7333 11:07:18, l.7543 11:09:21, l.7756 11:11:24: '3 asks for the whole picture answered (rs)'). So the cause is on the host.
- On Rapt0r's game the Alicorn copy was 'NOT removed (204 alive)' (13:03:12), so its pool addresses stayed occupied there.
- The R30 run, which had no Alicorn round, had 8 resyncs in 2 h.
- The host's notes: 'around wave 20ish, some clients mentioned desync'.
findings.cause:
hostPlane (sv_coop.lua:466 in 0.73.79, :505 at HEAD) returns early for any plane whose address is in SPC.alcnPool.set, whatever its unit. SPC.alcnPool (sv_alicorn.lua:60, 112-115) holds the 131 parked pools' addresses and is reset only at the next Alicorn spawn, never cleared.

Once the host destroyed the Alicorn's unit, the pools' memory was freed. New enemy planes reusing it were skipped: no 'bd', no stream, no 'dn'. u.n counts only the rest, so on joiners the later ordinals bind to the wrong host plane (a visible jump), and the last copy stays unbound. That copy flies its own AI for 15 s, is taken down as a stray and triggers 'jn'. The host's picture can't contain the skipped plane, so the loop repeats every 2-5 minutes, and the skipped planes exist only on the host.

clientPlane (0.73.79:1041, HEAD:1154) has the same check.

Inferred, because addresses aren't logged: that address reuse is what hit the set. The timing and the 'ids = N + N resent' counts fit it, and nothing else in hostPlane skips some planes of a unit but not all.
findings.fix: In hostPlane and clientPlane, check the unit before the set: `if unit == "SV_Unit_Alicorn" and SPC.alcnPool and a and SPC.alcnPool.set[a] then return end`. SPC.alicornPooled only ever records that unit's planes. Also set SPC.alcnPool = nil when the Alicorn's unit is removed (SPC.cleanTick, n <= 0 for it) and on a new level, and log once when hostPlane skips a plane.

verdicts.reason:
The evidence and the cause both hold. I'm marking this refuted only because it is already fixed at HEAD, by commit 8068e5c, which landed after the 0.73.82 patch.

Evidence, re-checked against the logs:
- **Clock offset is exactly 2:00.** Host 11:06:02 "ERA_Unit_02_Dep_Air1 ... 4 aircraft up" matches Rapt0r 13:06:02, where the same four f22a are created.
- **Rapt0r's log, before 13:06:21:** 0 stray lines and 0 "planes bound" lines. The only rs|j is at 12:08:06 (his join).
- **Rapt0r's log, after 13:06:21:**
  - 47 stray lines (86 copies).
  - 17 jn asks.
  - 53 partial-bind lines: 204 planes, 121 bound, 83 unbound.
  - About 109-112 aircraft flights spawned from 13:05:58.
- **Ids sent against planes created:**
  - ERB_Unit_01_Air2 gen 249 was spawned at 13:08:40, after the 13:08:34 repair. It shows "2 of 4 ... 2 for gen 249" with no resend in between, so the host sent only 2 bd.
  - On the host, all 4 planes were created and logged (11:08:41, #25-#28).
  - ERA_Unit_07_Dep_Air0 gen 237 got no bd at all ("last ids: 2 for gen 224").
  - Counts like 6 for gen 243 are 3 + 3, the second 3 resent by hostSync (0.73.79 sv_coop.lua:766). bl.n counts every bd received.
- **Only hostPlane can drop single planes here.** In 0.73.79, rawLogPlane (sv_core.lua:926-955) logs "AI aircraft created" and the logPlane wrapper (sv_coop.lua:4214-4227) then calls hostPlane. There are 0 "coop: plane error" lines.
  - hostPlane's only per-plane early return is `if SPC.alcnPool and a and SPC.alcnPool.set[a] then return end` (sv_coop.lua:466).
  - The `not u` return drops a whole unit, not single planes.
  - SPC.alicornPooled filters by unit, but the address set is never cleared after it.
- **Timing:**
  - Host 11:00:50: 131 pools put away.
  - 11:03:33: SV_Recycle of the Alicorn (204 alive).
  - Crumbs 11:04:03.850: its unit actor destroyed.
  - Round 20's wave 1 (11:03:36-59, before the destroy) bound fully. Wave 2 (11:05:59 on) is the first affected.
- **Host resync answers:** 3 in the whole session before 11:04 (1 in the 59 min before; the finding says 3 there, a small slip) and 62 after, in waves of 3-5 (every joiner at once), from 11:07:18 to 12:03:10.
- **Joiner's own Alicorn copy:** "NOT removed (204 alive)" at 13:03:12, so its pools stayed alive and the joiner-side check cannot fire.
- **Control runs:** R30 (no Alicorn round) had 8 resyncs in total. The 0.73.81 run (d_alessia) had no Alicorn round, so it neither confirms nor clears this.
- **What stays inferred:** addresses aren't logged, so address reuse itself isn't shown directly. Nothing else in the code can drop some planes of a unit and not others, though.

Fix at HEAD, commit 8068e5c "the Alicorn's pool addresses skip only its own planes and go with its unit" (WIP, not yet in a build or run in game). It does what the finding proposes:
- sv_coop.lua:518 (hostPlane) and :1188 (clientPlane) now require `unit == SPC.alicornUnit` before the set lookup.
- sv_rounds.lua:335 (SPC.cleanTick) drops SPC.alcnPool when the Alicorn's unit is removed (n <= 0).
- sv_alicorn.lua:12 drops it with the level (LEVEL_DROPS).
- sv_coop.lua:1451 (doSpawn) drops it when a joiner spawns the host's fresh Alicorn copy.
- poolTick only runs while the Alicorn sails, so stale sound-silencing isn't an issue.

The uncommitted working-tree changes keep the fix. The fix covers this case: enemy flights' units are never SV_Unit_Alicorn, so a reused address can no longer skip them.

The one piece of the proposal not built is a once-per-run log line when hostPlane skips a pooled plane. It would only help confirm the fix in game.
verdicts.corrected_status: The evidence and cause are confirmed. Fixed at HEAD by commit 8068e5c (after 0.73.82; WIP, not yet in a build or run in game). Not fixed in 0.73.80, 0.73.81 or 0.73.82. The 0.73.81 run (d_alessia) had no Alicorn round, so it can't show this.
verdicts.fix: Already at HEAD (8068e5c): `if unit == SPC.alicornUnit and SPC.alcnPool and a and SPC.alcnPool.set[a] then return end` in hostPlane (sv_coop.lua:518) and clientPlane (:1188). SPC.alcnPool = nil in SPC.cleanTick when its unit is removed (sv_rounds.lua:335), with the level (LEVEL_DROPS, sv_alicorn.lua:12), and when a joiner spawns a fresh Alicorn copy (sv_coop.lua:1451). Optional addition: a once-per-run log line when hostPlane skips a pooled plane, so the next Alicorn co-op test can confirm it. To check in game: after an Alicorn round, joiners show no "N of M planes bound" lines and no stray takedowns, and the host's "asks for the whole picture answered" stays near 0.

findings.title: A joiner's kills never count as the game's own: no DESTROYED and no kill score on the HUD's SCORE row (complaints 1 and 2)
findings.evidence:
Rapt0r lua log:
- l.446 '12:08:48 coop: copies held at 1.0 HP until the host's kill (the field written; MinHealth reads back 1.0)'.
- l.421-422 'player 1's real plane (falken) not spawned ... AI stand-in instead' and 'player 1's plane as f16c_common_svcp: spawned'.
- l.403 'hud: the game's score limit hidden': the game's own SCORE stays on screen.
- Floor clips: l.579 '12:11:12 copy 33 held at the floor, your missile at it gone ... its last health sent again'; l.3676 '12:56:03 a copy taken to the floor by your missile ... sent whole to the host'.
- l.1148 '12:20:21 a copy here couldn't be finished (health 10 after)' (a Spaceport boat copy, stuck at the floor).

All 117 of his own-kill pays match a host 'went down to player 4' within ±2 s (65 in the same second). His per-round own kills equal the host's player-4 counts in every round (r10 11/11, r14 14/14). Host 12:04:58 'Rapt0r 117/6/0'. So the kills were real and paid, but every one came from the host's 'dn', never his own weapon.

24 planes his copy's damage map shows he hit went to another player, e.g. 13:48:38 'f22a ... went down to player 5 (damage: you 100 ...)'.
findings.cause:
In 0.73.79, floorOn (sv_coop.lua:879-890) clamps every lethal hit at 1 HP, so the game shows HIT. The death comes from the 'dn' handler (3977-4003) via killCopy (903-938), with causer = hostPuppet() (here the host's AI F-16C stand-in) or nil.

Per KILLS_HEALTH_DEATH.md, the last-player-attacker record (+0x498) is set only for a LivePlayerPlane causer, and the per-kill score is credited to the attacker. So the game credits Rapt0r with nothing. Only the damage score from his clamped hits remains.

HEAD: M.dnKill (sv_coop.lua:1030-1052) passes his pawn when the dn's field 4 equals COOP.slot, which per the RE notes should give DESTROYED and kill score. It has never run on a joiner whose log we have: the 0.73.81 set is the host's only. The fallback [coop] kill_callout defaults to false (sv_config.lua:1269).

hostKiller (HEAD sv_coop.lua:571-591, unchanged) names the player with the most damage, not the last hit. So 'even if I got the final blow' still gives no DESTROYED at HEAD when someone else did more damage.
findings.fix: Next co-op test: on a joiner, read the CampaignInfo ScoreText (KILLS_HEALTH_DEATH.md 6) before and about 1 s after the first 5 'yours' M.dnKill calls, and log the change. Also log M.dnKill's once-line ('taken down here with your plane as its cause'). If the score doesn't move, set kill_callout = true by default. Optionally, keep the last joiner whose 'ht' landed before the death (e.lastBy) and name them in 'dn' instead of the most-damage player, to match the game's final-blow rule.

verdicts.reason:
The evidence and the cause are right, but HEAD already fixes the bug, so it isn't "new".

**Evidence holds.**
- The host log (a_31round, lines 5349 to 12917) and the joiner log (b_Logs, lines 3250 to 7347) have the same 9 'ROUND N KILLS' callouts, word for word, about 1 s apart. Example: host 10:49:35 'YOU 21 ALLIES 0 SHIPS 2' and joiner 12:49:35 'YOU 21 ALLIES 0 SHIPS 2'.
- The joiner log has no 'kills: round' lines of its own.
- I counted the joiner's own kills per round: 'credits: +N (... down (' lines with no ', by ', between the 'round N cleared (the host's round)' lines. The counts are r15 0, r17 5, r18 7, r20 0, r23 6, r24 4, r27 0, r29 4, r30 0. That matches the analyst. The shown 'YOU' was wrong in 8 of 9 rounds (only r30 was right: 0 = 0).

**Cause holds at the build that ran (0.73.79, commit 8bdc607).**
- sv_rounds.lua:1436 calls hudCallout(t.kills, ...) from the host's RUN.roundKills.
- The sv_coop.lua:4184-4186 wrapper sends every host callout without M.noMirror to the joiners as 'co'.
- The joiner resets its own RUN.roundKills (sv_coop.lua:1394) but never shows it.
- Patches 0.73.80 to 0.73.82 still have it: commit 21f8d41's sv_rounds.lua:1595 still calls hudCallout directly, and its sv_coop.lua has no localCallout.

**Already fixed at HEAD.** Commit 49bfdc2, '[claude] WIP, not yet run in game: the round's kills each game's own', labelled 0.73.83 and an ancestor of HEAD ba0abe4 on COOP2MP. It makes exactly the proposed fix:
- sv_coop.lua:170 adds COOP.localCallout, which sets M.noMirror.
- sv_rounds.lua:1697-1698 has the host show its own callout through it.
- sv_coop.lua:1574-1585 has each joiner, when the host's round goes to 'wait' (same round number), log 'kills: round N: ... (this game's)'. It then shows its own callout from RUN.roundKills, with the same allies + ships + defences > 0 condition. RUN.roundKills is reset when the round number changes (sv_coop.lua:1569).

**The fix covers this case.** In r15 Rapt0r's game counted 2 ship kills and 0 of his own, so it would show 'YOU 0 ... SHIPS 2'. In r30 his game had no ally, ship or defence kills, so it shows no callout, as the host does in such a round.

**Tests.** coop_ground_test.sh passes at HEAD, including:
- 'host: (0.73.83) the round's kills shown here, not sent to the joiners'
- 'join: (0.73.83) the host's round ends: its kills shown from this game's own count (ROUND 6 KILLS / YOU 4 ALLIES 2 ...)'
- 'join: ... none when only you shot anything down'

findings.title: Every VOID WATCHER removal froze its stream on joiners (held bursts) and left a ghost copy for 6-14 minutes
findings.evidence:

RE_SV_AwacsRemove fired') line up with all of Rapt0r's large held counts: '1324 held' 12:44:22, '231 held' 13:10:23, '194 held' 13:35:23, '60 held' 14:00:23. The ghost lasted until the next purchase: '12:58:01 coop: SV_Unit_VoidWatcher is up here (3 alive ...)' then '12:58:09 ... unstuck: still 3 alive here after 6 tries'. The same happened at 13:16:38/46 and 13:47:38. The copy was up 14, 6 and 12 minutes after each removal.

findings.fix: On a joiner, when the host's VOID WATCHER is removed (the 'ev' RE_SV_AwacsRemove, or a dn that fails on an ally copy): unbind it (SV_CoopBind(id,0)), hide it, switch collision and tick off, then SV_Recycle(unit, 2). In CoSample, clamp extrapolation to min(ahead, 0.5 s) so a copy never snaps back.

verdicts.reason:
The evidence holds and the cause is right, but the status is wrong. The repo HEAD is ba0abe4 (COOP2MP, after 0.73.82's 21f8d41), and that commit already fixes exactly this, citing B7. So the bug is fixed at HEAD and is not known-open.

Evidence, re-checked:
- **Clock offset.** The joiner's clock is the host's +2:00:00, within about 1 s. Host 10:43:59 "round 14: ERA_Unit_02_Dep_Air1 ... 4 aircraft up" matches joiner 12:43:59 "AI aircraft created #7" for the same flight.
- **Host removals.** All four are in a_31round AC8SurvivalMode_lua.log: l.4651 10:44:03, l.7642 11:10:18, l.10139 11:35:18, l.13174 12:00:21. Each time the host's native log shows "SV_Unit_VoidWatcher: its last flight was taken down (forced, aircraft still counted alive)" and "SV_Recycle, force 1" 2 s later (10:44:05, 11:10:20, 11:35:21, 12:00:23). So the host's copy also stays counted alive after the event.
- **Held counts.** Rapt0r's native log has nonzero held only at these lines: 823 12:44:22 "1324 held", 1347 13:10:23 "231 held", 1805 13:35:23 "194 held", 2253 13:58:23 "92 held", 2292 14:00:23 "60 held". Every other minute reads 0.
- **One stream fits.** Assume one stream held from the host's recycle (removal + 2 s) to each report, at the joiner's frame rate (player 3's real plane fed 4,900, 5,049, 4,639 and 4,726 frames in those minutes, about 77-84 fps). That gives about 17 s x 78 = 1,326 (seen 1,324), about 3 s x 84 = 252 (seen 231), about 3 s x 77 = 231 (seen 194) and about 1 s x 79 = 79 (seen 60).
- **Why the next minute reads 0.** The joiner's crumbs show its copy (ids 361-363) "taken down (forced)" only when the host's dn came: 12:44:27, 13:11:13, 13:36:19 and 14:00:46, that is 24, 55, 61 and 25 s after each removal. That unbinds the stream, and coop.c's minute report counts only bound streams (coop.c:1378). This is why the next minute always shows 0.
- **Ghost confirmed.** The joiner logs "SV_Unit_VoidWatcher is up here (3 alive ...)" and "unstuck: still 3 alive here after 6 tries" at 12:58:01/09, 13:16:38/46 and 13:47:30/38. That is 14, 6 and 12 minutes after the removals.

Two small corrections:
- The 92 at 13:58:23 came at VALKA's reveal ("decoys down, VALKA attacks" and "AB.L..IN gone: hidden" at host 11:57:26-30), not after she went down.
- The "ghost" is a copy switched off by LiveSetActiveGameObject false that still counts alive. The logs don't show it was visible.

Cause: as R30 verified. The forwarded RE_SV_AwacsRemove (survival_events.py:1855) switches the joiner's copy off before the host's dn arrives, and killCopy (sv_coop.lua:903 at 0.73.79) then can't finish it. The host stops streaming the copy at its removal, apparently at its SV_Recycle 2 s later, so the joiner keeps driving the copy at its last state until the dn unbinds it.

The claim that "neither the removal path nor coop.c changed" holds through 0.73.82: no coop.c commit since 294712f. It no longer holds at HEAD:
- **Host side.** sv_allies.lua:913 calls COOP.removeNow(u) before SV_Event(hm.remove). Defined at sv_coop.lua:637-653, it sends dn|<id>|r (unpaid, reliable) for each of the unit's objects, marks them dead and calls SV_CoopTrack(id, 0).
- **Ordering.** Reliable messages arrive in order (coop.c CO_OOO/recvNext), so each joiner's dn handler runs killCopy(torn, force) on a copy that is still active and unbinds it before the event switches it off. R30 showed a forced takedown of an active E-767 copy works.
- **Joiner side.** hostEvent (sv_coop.lua:1534-1551) takes down any copy still bound, clears cu.planes and calls SV_Recycle(unit, alive>0 and 1 or 0) 2 s later (COOP.tick, sv_coop.lua:5687-5702). That removes both the held stream and the minutes-long ghost.
- **Tests.** I ran tools/checks/coop_ground_test.sh at HEAD and it passes. It has the host check "VOID WATCHER taken off: its copy's dn sent at once, unpaid (-1>dn|15|r|)" and the joiner checks "the host's RE_SV_AwacsRemove: its copy here taken down and forgotten" and "its unit off this game's list 2 s on (SV_Unit_VoidWatcher:1)".

The proposed CoSample clamp isn't needed for B7, because the stream is unbound before it would hold. It is R30's separate snap-back point.

Still open:

The evidence holds, and the cause is right in substance. But current HEAD (ba0abe4, WIP 0.73.83, committed after 0.73.82) already carries a fix written for exactly this finding ("B7, verified twice"), so "known-open" is wrong.

What I checked in the logs:
- **Clock offset.** Rapt0r's clock is the host's + 1:59:59.2. The same spawn is at host 10:44:02.960 and joiner 12:44:02.215, and at 10:44:06.040 vs 12:44:05.269.

Every other minute shows 0 held, except 92 at 13:58:23, after VALKA died (host 11:58:02).
- **When the hold starts.** It starts at the host's SV_Recycle, about 2.1 s after the event (crumbs 10:44:05.675, 11:10:20.751, 11:35:21.217, 12:00:23.132), not at the event itself. At the joiner's ~80 fps (4600-5000 frames fed a minute), one stream held from recycle to report gives about 1320 / 230 / 200 / 0-84 moves. That matches 1324 / 231 / 194 / 60.
- **How long it really lasted.** The hold ran on until the host's dn reached the joiner: crumbs 'copy BP_OP0005_e767_CP_Ally_C_... taken down (id 361, forced)' at 12:44:27, then 13:11:13, 13:36:19 and 14:00:46. That is 24-61 s after each removal. The next minute's reports show 0 held only because the stream was unbound before them, so its held moves were never summed (coop.c reports bound entries only). The real hold was longer than the counts suggest.
- **The ghost.** The same three objects (…_2147399487/86/84) were taken down again at 12:58:01 ('torn'). The unit then stayed '3 alive' until the next purchase forced it off: 'unstuck: still 3 alive here after 6 tries' at 12:58:09, 13:16:46 and 13:47:38. Resyncs also tore it down at 13:16:12, 13:40:09 and 14:02:24 ('SV_Unit_VoidWatcher (3)'). That is 14, 6 and 12 minutes. 'Alive' here means on the spawner list; the logs can't show whether it was visible.
- **The cause.** In 0.73.79 (1717cef), sv_coop.lua mirrors RE_SV_AwacsRemove (it is not in KEEP_EVENTS) and hostEvent fires it raw on the joiner. Nothing there unbinds or recycles the copy. The host alone recycles it, and its own native log says 'aircraft still counted alive'. 0.73.80-0.73.82 didn't touch this.

How HEAD covers it:
- **The held stream.** In sv_allies.lua:913, awacsService now calls COOP.removeNow(u) before SV_Event. COOP.removeNow (sv_coop.lua:637-653) sends 'dn|<id>|r' for every copy of the unit, unpaid, and calls SV_CoopTrack(id, 0). Reliable messages are delivered in order per link (coop.c l.16, 742-752), so each joiner's dn → M.dnKill → killCopy → SV_CoopBind(id, 0) runs before the event switches the copy off, and nothing is left to hold.
- **The ghost.** hostEvent (sv_coop.lua:1534-1551) kills any VOID WATCHER copy still bound, empties cunits[unit].planes, so a resync no longer finds stale planes, and queues SV_Recycle(unit, 1) 2 s on, which COOP.tick runs (sv_coop.lua:5687-5701). The unit leaves the joiner's spawner list as it leaves the host's, so the next purchase isn't stuck.
- **Tests.** I ran tools/checks/coop_ground_test.sh: 'host: all passed' (including 'VOID WATCHER taken off: its copy's dn sent at once, unpaid') and 'join: all passed' (copy taken down on the event, 'SV_Unit_VoidWatcher:1' recycled 2 s on).

**Status:** fixed at HEAD but not yet run in game. Watch for 'coop: the host took SV_Unit_VoidWatcher off ... 0 copies here' and 'off this game's spawner list ... SV_Recycle', and expect 0 held at each removal.
