verdicts.reason:
I confirmed the finding from the logs and the code, with one correction: the cost grows with the length of the spawner's phase unit list, not with the world's AI object count.

What holds:
- **Per-call cost (d_alessia).** Each lua.log natives line divided out (ms a tick / calls a tick) gives 0.73/1.1 = 0.66 ms (12:45:39), then 0.90, 1.27, 1.60, 1.69, 2.15, 2.46, 2.60, and 7.71/2.7 = 2.86 ms (13:26:29).
- **Spawn counts.** The native log's 'spawn X: up' lines reach 2, 15, 22, 30, 41, 67, 80, 105 and 111 at those times, as the finding says.
- **AI object counts.** The STORE minigame lines read 32 (native line 278), 118 (553), 132 (698), 144 (827) and 150 (880), as quoted.
- **Code.** survival_rt.c:1517 UnitAlive calls RegisteredUnit (:1378), which walks PhaseUnits() and runs Readable (VirtualQuery, :221) on each entry. UnitId runs a second Readable on the vtable slot. The code is identical in 0.32.23 (the run's runtime, :1514/:1375/:218) and at HEAD (0.32.24 only dropped the log flush and added SV_PPWeapons).

The correction (the title's "tracks the world's AI object count", ~20 us per object):
- **What the list holds.** The phase list keeps one entry per distinct unit spawned. Counting 'spawn X: up' minus 'took it off the phase's list' gives 2, 8, 10, 13, 18, 25, 26, 29 and 31 entries at the nine perf times. That is about 76 us per entry, the same ~75 us R30 measured on the same PC.
- **c_casual44 tells the two models apart.** That log has LogUnits lines and minigame counts. Alicorn round 23 ran 00:44:06-01:13:21. The AI objects went 197 -> 423 (00:44:29, 00:50:17, 01:08:27: 131 pooled aircraft plus parts). The logged phase list went only 39 -> 40. Per-call cost stayed flat: 1.76 (00:44), 1.81, 1.73, 1.63 ms (01:05). At 20 us per object it would have risen by about 4.5 ms. Over that whole run, cost follows the logged list (1 -> 58 entries, 0.73 -> ~2.05 ms).
- **The per-object slope isn't stable.** In a_31round it was 39 us early and 23 us late.
- **The finding understates the total cost.** At 13:26 SV_UnitAlive took 7.71 ms a tick, 42% of the 18.5 ms tick. ALIVE made only part of the calls: its round 14 line shows 1786 asks in 380 s, about 4.7 a second or ~3.3 ms a tick. Callers outside ALIVE made the rest (leave check 1.3 ms a tick, allies/counts 1.3).
- **a_31round's late cost is higher than quoted.** It ran 7.0-7.4 ms a call from 11:22, not 6.6.

Status at HEAD: known-open, partly mitigated. WIP commit 99209a3 (0.73.83, not yet run in game) cuts the asks made outside ALIVE. It also takes a special's units off the list after its round. The native walk is unchanged, though. Pool flights stay on the list (22 of d_alessia's 31 entries, 24-25 in the other runs), and so do the STORE allies and defences (9 others in d_alessia). So late per-call cost on her PC stays around 2.5-3 ms.
verdicts.corrected_status: known-open (native per-call O(phase-list) walk unchanged at HEAD; WIP 99209a3 only cuts some asks and removes specials' units from the list). Driver is the phase unit list length (~75 us/entry on Saint Alessia's PC, ~23 us on the casual44 PC), not the AI object count.
verdicts.fix:
Native fix, in runtime/survival_rt.c RegisteredUnit (:1378):
1. **Remember where each unit sits.** Keep a small table keyed by desc UniqueID holding {unit, idx}. Before walking, read PhaseUnits() and return the cached unit when idx < num, data[idx] == unit and UnitId(unit) == id. This never dereferences a pointer the list no longer holds. Walk only on a miss, and refill the entry from the walk. Clear the table in Recycle, in SV_Reset and at the teardown gate.
2. **Drop the per-entry VirtualQuery in the walk.** Test each entry with UObjAllocated(u) == 1, falling back to Readable only when it answers -1 (GUObjectArray not found). In UnitId, replace Readable(vt + slot) with a range check against the exe image (g_exe .. g_exe + SizeOfImage).
3. **Log the list length.** Return or log PhaseUnits()->num through a cheap native (or on the natives perf line), so the next test shows cost per entry. LogUnits is verbose-only since 0.73.79.

Optional: remember FindDesc's answer per FName.

Until a runtime build ships, keep 99209a3's Lua levers. A further Lua stopgap is to take STORE defence and ally units off the list once they're down, as 99209a3 does for specials.

verdicts.reason:
I confirmed this from the logs and the code. One correction: the cost tracks the number of units on the spawner's list, not the world's AI object count.

Per-call numbers, d_alessia (AC8SurvivalMode_lua.log, the natives part of each `perf: lists:` line, ms a tick divided by calls a tick):

| Time | Line | ms a tick / calls | ms a call |
|---|---|---|---|
| 12:45:39 | 523 | 0.73 / 1.1 | 0.66 |
| 12:50:45 | 870 | 1.17 / 1.3 | 0.90 |
| 12:55:51 | 1213 | 2.29 / 1.8 | 1.27 |
| 13:00:58 | 1570 | 2.24 / 1.4 | 1.60 |
| 13:06:04 | 2014 | 3.05 / 1.8 | 1.69 |
| 13:11:10 | 2666 | 4.72 / 2.2 | 2.15 |
| 13:16:17 | 3295 | 7.39 / 3.0 | 2.46 |
| 13:21:24 | 4019 | 5.20 / 2.0 | 2.60 |
| 13:26:29 | 4505 | 7.71 / 2.7 | 2.86 |

- The spawn counts before each line are 2/15/22/30/41/67/80/105/111, as the analyst says.
- The minigame counts in AC8SurvivalMode.log are right: line 278 has 32, 553 has 118, 698 has 132, 827 has 144, 880 has 150.
- a_31round: 0.68 ms a call at 10:03 and 0.77 at 10:08. It reached 4.1 at 10:24:38, 6.0 at 10:29, and 6.6-7.25 from 11:01 to 11:54. The AI object count went 48 → 298, as stated.

The analyst undersold the size of it. The measured total at 13:26:29 is 7.71 ms a tick, which is 42% of the 18.5 ms tick, not 3.6 ms. That is 2.7 calls a tick, about 10.8 a second.
- ALIVE made about 4.7 of those a second: round 14 had 1786 asks from 13:20:28 to 13:26:48.
- The rest come from asks outside ALIVE. The parts that make them grew with the per-call cost: leave check 0.3 → 1.3 ms and allies/counts 0.2 → 1.3 ms.

The better predictor is the number of units on the list:
- A shot-down unit stays registered until its desc spawns again (Recycle runs only inside Spawn). So the list holds every distinct unit spawned so far.
- d_alessia had 2/8/10/13/18/25/26/29/31 distinct units at those nine times. That fits a straight line of about 0.5 ms plus 75 µs a unit.
- a_31round fits the same slope, about 80 µs a unit. Its jump from 1.85 to 4.1 ms came exactly as the Spaceport's 27 ships and 5 LCAC units came onto the list (10:19:41-10:23:11), taking it from 16 to 49 units.
- Divided per AI object instead, the two runs disagree: 17-19 µs in d_alessia and 24-31 µs in a_31round, not the 19-22 µs the analyst gives for both. The AI object count only grows alongside the unit count.

The cause is right. runtime/survival_rt.c:1517 UnitAlive calls RegisteredUnit (:1378), which walks PhaseUnits(). For every entry it calls Readable(u), which is a VirtualQuery system call (:221), and UnitId (:1370), which makes a second Readable on the vtable. A unit not on the list costs a full walk.
- About 75 µs an entry fits two VirtualQuery calls on a process with about 31 GB committed.
- The fixed part of each call fits the same picture: SpawnerReady, PhaseUnits and UnitArrayNum make about 6 more Readable calls. SV_Event costs about 0.3 ms a call the same way.

It is not fixed at HEAD, so the status stays known-open:
- `git diff 294712f HEAD -- runtime/survival_rt.c` (runtime 0.32.23 to HEAD) leaves Readable, PhaseUnits, UnitId, RegisteredUnit and UnitAlive unchanged.
- HEAD's commit 99209a3 (a work-in-progress 0.73.83, not yet run in game) only eases it from Lua. It makes fewer asks outside ALIVE (airUp, the allies' share, the leave probe every 5 s, co-op's check, the director). It also takes a special's units off the list after its round, via SPC.recycleLater / SV_Recycle(unit, 0).
- In d_alessia, 99209a3 would remove only 3 of the 31 units (SV_Unit_Glitch, LadonKot, LadonMishka). The 22 pool flights, 4 defences, VOID WATCHER and MOONCHILD stay, so each call would still cost about 2.6 ms by round 14. The cost per entry is untouched.
verdicts.corrected_status: known-open (partly eased by HEAD's work-in-progress commit 99209a3, not yet run in game; the native cost per entry is unchanged at HEAD)
verdicts.fix:
Native fix, smallest at HEAD: stop making a system call for each entry of the walk. The engine's object table (GUObjectArray) was found in this run (native log line 38: "guard: GUObjectArray chunks at ...").
- In RegisteredUnit (survival_rt.c:1378), test each entry with `int ok = UObjAllocated(u); if (ok < 0) ok = u && Readable(u, LY.idIface + 8);` and go on only when ok == 1. This reads the object table, not VirtualQuery.
- In UnitId (:1370), replace `Readable(vt + LY.idSlot/8, 8)` with `InGame(vt + LY.idSlot/8)`, since vtables live in the exe image.
- That cuts about 2 VirtualQuery calls an entry, roughly 75 µs each.
- Optional: keep the unit pointer per desc. Set it in Spawn, which already gets it from g_spawnUnit, and clear it in Recycle. Check it with UObjAllocated == 1 and UnitId == id, and walk only on a miss.

To confirm the cause, add PhaseUnits()->num to the `alive: round N` line or the perf line. For example, have SV_LogUnits return the length without logging every unit, or add a small SV_UnitCount.

Lua stopgap until a native build: keep HEAD's 99209a3 and cap ALIVE's budget by measured cost, for example at most about 1.5 ms of SV_UnitAlive a tick. A plane seen down still asks at once.

The jump is real, but the cause and the fix are wrong.

What holds (d_alessia AC8SurvivalMode_lua.log 1418-1518, UE4SS.log 2449-2527): BP_OP0011_tu95_CP_C_2147439427 (k 2, given RE_SV_HeavyLoop_04CE at 12:58:18.46) read 24.4 km out and 6.8 km up at 12:58:51.18. By 12:59:21.84, 30.7 s later, it read 6.6 km, closest 6.2 km. bombTick refreshes p.closest every second (sv_flights.lua:105-123 at 36c2b03), so 6.2 km was a real sample. Getting there means at least 18.2 km in 30.7 s, about 2,140 km/h, against HEAVY_SPEED 850. Very likely farther: sector E's loop starts 6 km north of the airfield and the plane was still south of it. After that it held 2.0 km and read 11.5 km at 12:59:52, which fits flying the loop from its first point (6.0, 9.2, then 11.5 km out). One overstatement: the 2.3 km climb in 31 s is not a jump. That is 74 m/s at 236 m/s, an 18-degree climb.

Why the cause is wrong:
1. **The timing doesn't fit an execution-time warp.** g.execute clears Delay (survival_events.py:1126-1127), and build_heavy passes none (:1514). Yet 2.2 s after the event the plane was 19.5 km out. 33 s after, it was 24.4 km out, moving away from the loop start and 4.8 km above the loop's height. The move came 33-63 s after the event, about 60 s on (12:58:18.5 + 60 = 12:59:18.5; 3.3 s at 236 m/s from the first point gives about 6.6 km). Nothing Survival fired lies in that window: UE4SS.log 2496-2511 has only round and ammo lines, and the crumbs have nothing between 12:57:36 and 13:00:30.
2. **The same template never warped other planes.** The same record (Mission 16's PathFinish_Ladon0_0, with the same {0 object, 2 path, 4 speed} changes) also drove VOID WATCHER's orbit (RE_SV_AwacsOrbit, commit 9541541 build_awacs) and the Ladons' circuits. VOID WATCHER flew straight to 163 km over 21 minutes with RE_SV_AwacsOrbit firing, and MISHKA flew 87 km off (HOTFIX_NOTES.md:44-49). The 0.73.74 Ladons held their old tangent to 29 km out. None of them warped.
3. **There is no warp flag to turn off.** The usmap gives LiveAIPathExecution no reflected properties. Path teleports are separate classes (LiveAIPathTeleportByDistanceExecution / ByPointExecution), and build_heavy doesn't use them.

Impact is also overstated. The move put the bomber onto its loop, closer to the airfield. It missed the 3 km drop distance because it was shot down 52 s later (13:00:10), about 91 s of loop short of the runway crossing. The real defect is the minute before: it didn't fly the loop it was handed, the same open problem as HOTFIX_NOTES problem 2 and hard rule 54 (a path that doesn't start near the plane, ahead of it, isn't flown). Its being snapped onto the loop is the game's own doing, mechanism unknown. One candidate: the heavies keep the stock MaxAltitudeInMeter (build_survival.py:1224-1231 sets only the radius), and it had climbed to 6.8 km. a_31round's takers were all near the loop start, so it can't be compared there. build_heavy and heavyNext are unchanged since 0.73.81, so this is still open at HEAD.

The cause is still unknown, so this is not a new execution bug.

The smallest fix at HEAD is in sv_flights.lua heavyNext: hand over only when the new taker is within about 8 km of its loop's first point, measured from its own position. verdicts.fix:
In mod/UE4SS/AC8SurvivalMode/Scripts/sv_weaponlog.lua:306-316, walk one base a pass after the first look, so each tick half pays one ~35 ms walk instead of three:

```lua
if now >= (R.walkAt or 0) then
    local list = R.walkAt and { BASES[(R.walkI or 0) % #BASES + 1] } or BASES   -- (the first look primes all three)
    if R.walkAt then R.walkI = (R.walkI or 0) % #BASES + 1 end
    R.walkAt = now + WALK_S / #BASES          -- (each base still every WALK_S)
    for _, base in ipairs(list) do
        local okF, found = pcall(FindAllOf, base)
        for _, w in ipairs(okF and found or {}) do
            local a = liveAddr(w)
            if a and not R.pool[a] then R.pool[a] = { obj = w, base = base } end
        end
    end
    R.walks = (R.walks or 0) + 1
end
```

NotifyOnNewObject already feeds WLOG.new for all three bases (:44-48). The walk is only a backstop for items the queue dropped (NEW_MAX) or made before the run, so WALK_S can also go up to 120-300 s. That cuts the walks' total cost too, not just the hitch.

- playerOnAirfield (sv_rounds.lua:1346-1351) is any point within 3 km of the airfield and under 100 m, so a relabel first runs on the approach, before the landing menu exists.

verdicts.reason:
The numbers hold and the problem is still open at HEAD, but the cause the finding gives is incomplete and partly misplaced.

**Numbers re-checked.** d_alessia/AC8SurvivalMode_lua.log:
- `shop` worst 135/123/192/149/183 ms (lines 1212, 1569, 2665, 3294, 4018).
- `shop/presses` worst 51/161/49/153 ms.
- `shop/texts` worst 135/74/98/100/93 ms.
- At 13:11:10 (line 2666): `TextBlock 12x 440 ms (1063 found)` and `WBP_Menu_IngameHangar_WeaponDetail_002_C 13x 484 ms`.
- a_31round `shop` worst runs 118-268 ms.
- No FUObjectHashTables: UE4SS.log:622.

**The root cause the finding missed: a latched fallback (new).** 0.73.77 (B4) already keeps the STORE rows' TextBlocks (SH.rowTexts, keyed by the landing windows). That path never ran in any of the five logs: none has `the STORE rows' N TextBlocks kept`. In every log the first relabel trips the fallback `shop: no STORE row TextBlock under a WBP_Menu_Text_Focus row; row labels are looked for in every TextBlock`:
- a_31round 10:10:54
- b_Logs 12:13:22
- d_alessia 12:54:12
- c_casual44 22:16:47
- e_loose 06:32:59

How it trips:
1. playerOnAirfield() (sv_rounds.lua:1346) is true anywhere within 3 km of the airfield and below 100 m. In d_alessia the gear came down at 12:54:10, the latch fired at 12:54:12, and `on the ground at your airfield` only came at 12:54:19.
2. A kill sets RUN.dirty, so shopTexts runs and calls relabel before any landing page exists. SHOP.windowsKey is "", the walk finds no Text_Focus TextBlock, and rows == 0.
3. sv_shop.lua:485 then sets `SH.relabelAll = true`. SH is made once per session (sv_flights.lua:489) and never reset.

From then on, every relabel walks every TextBlock, reads all ~600-1000 names and calls GetText on every transient one. UE4SS.log shows each press's `BOUGHT` line followed by its relabel 88-98 ms later:
- 13:10:33.527 → .624
- 13:21:18.282 → .370
- 13:21:18.602 → .694
- 13:21:18.906 → .994
- 13:21:19.560 → .649

That cost is counted in `shop/texts`, not `shop/presses`.

**Corrections to the stated cause.**
- `shop/presses` (161/153 ms) holds no TextBlock walk. It is SHOP.pressPage's walk of WBP_Menu_IngameHangar_Common_000_C, about 40 ms each, after a press on a page not kept (`a STORE press 7` at 13:10:53, `6` at 13:21:38), plus the purchase itself. SV_Spawn's worst was 76 ms in the 13:11 window, from the CIWS, SAM and AA builds at 13:10:33-35.
- The WeaponDetail_002_C walks and about half the TextBlock walks belong to the separate `ammo panel` part (sv_main.lua:45 and :86; worst 77-97 ms), not to `shop`.

**Not fixed at HEAD.** relabel, LANDW and the ammo panel are unchanged since 36c2b03 (0.73.81). The latch is still at sv_shop.lua:485 and still never reset.
verdicts.corrected_status: known-open. The relabel walking every TextBlock on every flush is a new bug: SH.relabelAll latches on the first approach to the airfield and never resets, which turns off the 0.73.77 kept-TextBlocks path.
verdicts.fix:
Two steps, both in sv_shop.lua at HEAD.

1) Stop the latch (one-liners in relabel()):
- After `local key = (not all) and SHOP.windowsKey(SH.tick) or nil`, add `if key == "" then return nil end`. With no landing window kept (the approach inside 3 km and below 100 m), the queue waits: relabelFlush already puts it back on nil.
- Before `SH.relabelAll = true`, add `if not landingShown(SH.tick) then return nil end`. Only a page on screen with no Text_Focus TextBlock proves the filter wrong.
- Clear `SH.relabelAll = nil` in LEVEL_DROPS.store.

This turns the B4 kept path back on: a TextBlock walk only when the window key changes, and GetText only on the ~30 Text_Focus TextBlocks, not every transient one.

2) Walk-free, so a press needs no FindAllOf("TextBlock"):
- Take the label TextBlocks from the kept, visible LANDW windows by the path SHOP.decorTick already uses: child(win, "WBP_Menu_Pause_List_000") → child(list, "WBP_Menu_Text_Focus_000_0k") → child(row, "HorizontalBox_59"):GetAllChildren(), checking each with liveObj.
- Optionally let hangarAmmoTick's slotTexts reuse one TextBlock name list per tick with relabel instead of its own walk.

What step 2 leaves in `shop/presses`: pressPage's Common_000_C walk, which is about 40 ms after a press on a page not kept, and the purchase's own SV_Spawn.

analysts.summary:
Sets: c_casual44 is Nada's solo Casual run on the 0.73.78 friends' zip (hash 03e468eb, runtime 0.32.23). e_loose is Copperpug's first-ever run, solo on Ace, on the same zip.

c_casual44 timeline. Game started 20:54. SP ONLINE was picked at 21:01, but the difficulty page sat idle until 21:33. The level loaded at 21:34:15 on Casual, flying the Su-57. Rounds 1-44 ran until a one-hit death at 04:08:08, then a Retry at 04:08:16 and a quit. The 6:34 on the clock includes 5,638 s paused across 236 pauses and 14,104 s flown, with 42 landings.

Specials:
- r6 shuttle launched (+7,200).
- r8 and r33 amphibious repelled.
- r15 Ladons, both down in 292 s.
- r23 Alicorn sunk after 1,254 s; it dived 3 more times after its core opened.
- r28 and r41 MINDRIPPER down (67 s and 143 s).
- r37 VALKA down after 743 s; your health fell to 16%.
- Shuttle rounds 19, 30 and 43 never spawned and ran as plain rounds: 'not spawned (its last flight is still up)'.
- Ace squadrons in r16, 22, 25, 31, 34 and 40.

Totals: 957 kills of your own (1,207 air kills incl. allies' and ships', plus 38 ground). Earned 774,380 Z, spent 750,370 Z. The leaderboard accepted the run (200), but scored it 140,700 where the game said 142,950: the Worker ignores VALKA.

Main new problems, all still at HEAD:
1. On Casual, SV_Ammo answered -1 for the 20 s Lua tries it, in both levels, and then gave up for good. Every ammo-dependent system stayed off:
   - no caps or free-restock change;
   - 60 STORE ammo presses refused with 'NOT AVAILABLE YET';
   - WEAPON BAYS sold for 12,000 Z with no effect;
   - FLARE PODS undone at each landing;
   - no shot ever counted. That is why the learning line says 'missiles 0, gun 0, of 0 with a weapon seen', and all 1,207 kill lines say 'you fired nothing seen'.
   Every one of the other 20 logged sessions (Hard/Ace, Su-57 included) read ammo fine.
2. SECOND CHANCE only re-applies its floor when the game resets MinHealth in co-op (the reset check needs fl > 0). Solo, the 50,000 Z floor set at 02:12 was never re-written after the airfield stops that reset it. The final 615-HP drop was most likely a crash, which may bypass MinHealth anyway.
3. Two perf costs that grow over the run and are still in the HEAD code:
   - VOID WATCHER's ESM field list grows by one each launch (10 → 181) and is never pruned. It is walked every tick: SV_ObjChain calls went 25 → 403 a tick.
   - The between-rounds repair walks 7 classes once STORE ships and defences are up: a 164-187 ms hitch at every round clear from round 16 (63-74 ms before).
4. The restart check lets the rest of the tick run, so a pause-menu Restart pays and announces a fake 'round 1 clear' on the dead run.

Known and still open: SV_UnitAlive's per-call cost grows with the phase list (0.73 → 2.1 ms a call; 16 ms of a 28 ms tick at round 39). 0.73.80's cache cuts the number of calls, but the native fix isn't in yet.

Known and fixed later (0.73.79/0.73.80): the shuttle not recycled, specials pacing (shuttle picked 4 times; glitch and spaceport 0 times in 44 rounds), the Alicorn diving after its core opened, the fixed-cost parts, and walks of landing windows and VALKA rounds. Tier 1 is confirmed against the 0.73.81 run: clock 4.2 → 0.1 ms, rows watch 1.9 → 0.1 ms.

Perf over the run: the tick averaged 9-13 ms in rounds 1-9 and 17-35 ms in rounds 16-44. The worst half was 200-392 ms in every 5-minute window from round 17. No Lua errors and no crash in 7 h.

e_loose: Copperpug paused at 06:24:41.99 and picked the pause menu's Restart. The run started over in the same world at 06:24:44 after 37 s of round 1, with health at 81% after two round-1 QAAM hits. They then played rounds 1-4 normally, paused at 06:37:44 and closed the game. The Lua loop was still ticking at 06:41:01 and there is no crash trace. On Ace all 25 kills had a weapon seen, which confirms the attribution chain works when SV_Ammo reads.

Native side: runtime/survival_rt.c AmmoGet → PlayerWeapons (~L1626) returned NULL with AM.state=1, which is SV_ERR_NOT_READY. findings.sessions: c_casual44 (cause shown with co-op logs r30_host_SaintAlessia, r14_host 0.73.81)
findings.evidence:
In c_casual44 L10414/L10417, at 02:12:11: 'Insurance: SECOND CHANCE HELD for 50000', then 'insurance: your aircraft's floor 25.2 HP (SECOND CHANCE held)'. No other insurance line follows until the level ends.

The game resets MinHealth at the same airfield exit as MaxHealth. In r30_host_SaintAlessia at 19:19:17, 'upgrades: the game put your airframe back to 138 HP (an airfield stop)' and 'insurance: your aircraft's floor was put back by the game; 0.1 HP again (2 times)' land in the same second (also 18:52:59 right after a REARM). That is seen in 10 co-op logs.

Death at 04:08:08 (L16678): '-615 HP in 1 hit, health now 0%, SHOT DOWN; missiles near: none', nearest enemy 1.83 km, with SECOND CHANCE still held and never used. That 615 HP isn't in the plane's own damage record (the death line's 'record: ... x40a_CP_Tewy 529, f35c 85, f22a 79'), so it was probably a crash. findings.cause:
sv_tactical.lua INS.tick L458 (HEAD, the same since 060da12): `if fl > 0 and INS.min == want and INS.pawn == addrOf(pawn) then` reads MinHealth back only when co-op's revive floor (fl) is on. Solo, fl = 0, so a MinHealth the game zeroes at an airfield stop is never seen.

The MaxHealth reset (360) is undone by UP.healthGuard before INS.tick sees it (no 'floor 14.4 HP' line), so `want` never changes and the field is never written again.
findings.fix: In INS.tick, change the condition to `if want > 0 and INS.min == want and INS.pawn == addrOf(pawn) then` so the field is checked and re-written whenever a floor is wanted, solo included. Optionally, when the drop leaves no new entry in the plane's DamageHistoryMap, have the death line say 'crash?' instead of 'gun/close'. Note that a crash may bypass MinHealth (KILLS_HEALTH_DEATH.md), so this fix might not have saved this particular death.

findings.title: SV_UnitAlive's per-call cost grows with the phase list in solo too: by round 33+ it is over half of the tick
findings.evidence:
From the 'perf: lists' natives:
- r1 (21:35): 2.1 calls a tick, 1.53 ms (0.73 ms a call).
- r10 (23:12): 3.8 calls, 4.60 ms.
- r20 (00:13): 3.4 calls, 5.96 ms.
- r33 (02:17): 7.8 calls, 15.51 ms.
- r39 (03:23): 7.6 calls, 16.22 ms (2.1 ms a call) of a 28.0 ms tick.

The phase list in the native log grows from 1 unit (r1) to 57-58 (r38-44); 401 recycles.

The 'leave check' part (one SV_UnitAlive per tick half in 0.73.78) grows 1.3 → 6.4 ms a tick, and allies/counts 0.2 → 2.9 ms.

In the 0.73.81 co-op run (d_alessia), calls are down to 1.1-3.0 a tick, but a call costs 2.6 ms by round 14 (5.20 ms / 2.0).
findings.cause: Native SV_UnitAlive walks the spawner's list with VirtualQuery checks, so each call costs more the more units have ever been spawned (R30_FINDINGS perf 'Root cause'). runtime/survival_rt.c has no UnitAlive change since 294712f (the 0.32.24 diff is 11 lines, none of them here). Lua callers: rounds, ALLY.alive, and the leave probe in sv_core.lua L416-425 (SV_UnitAlive(CFG.pool[1]) twice a second at HEAD).
findings.fix: As R30 proposes: in the runtime, cache desc → unit pointer at SV_Spawn, clear it at Recycle and at the teardown gate, and check it with UObjLive (O(1)). In the meantime, have the leave probe ask a cheap native (SpawnerReady or SV_LevelGone) instead of SV_UnitAlive(pool[1]).

verdicts.reason:
Confirmed from the logs and the code, with three corrections.

Evidence (c_casual44/AC8SurvivalMode_lua.log, the `perf: lists` natives):
- Every quoted figure is in the log: L431 21:35 "SV_UnitAlive 2.1 a tick 1.53 ms", L2313 23:12 "3.8 a tick 4.60 ms", L5164 00:13 "3.4 a tick 5.96 ms", L10713 02:17 "7.8 a tick 15.51 ms", L14322 03:23:40 "7.6 a tick 16.22 ms" against L14321's "tick avg 28.0 ms".
- The cost of one call grows with the length of the phase's list. The list (AC8SurvivalMode.log "units (round N start)") goes 1 (r1) → 20 (r9) → 37 (r20) → 53 (r33) → 57-58 (r38-44).
- Measured cost per call: 0.70-0.98 ms at 1-15 units, 1.21 ms at 20-22, 1.75 ms at 37, 2.0 ms at 51-53, 2.13 ms at 57. That is about 0.65 ms fixed plus about 26 µs per list entry.
- "leave check" goes 1.3 → 6.4 ms a tick (02:53) and "allies/counts" 0.2 → 2.9 ms, as stated.
- In d_alessia (0.73.81) a call costs 0.66 ms at 12:45 (1.1 a tick, 0.73 ms), 2.6 ms at 13:21 (2.0 a tick, 5.20 ms) and 2.86 ms at 13:26. ALIVE logs about 10 native asks a second ("alive: round 14: 1786 native asks").

Code:
- runtime/survival_rt.c:1517 UnitAlive does SpawnerReady, then FindDesc, then RegisteredUnit (:1378), then UnitArrayNum.
- RegisteredUnit walks the phase's list until the id matches. For each entry it does Readable(u) (a VirtualQuery) plus UnitId (:1370: a Readable on the vtable slot and a virtual call). That is 2 syscalls and a call per entry.
- The only change to survival_rt.c since 294712f is the 0.32.24 diff (version, log flush, the SV_PPWeapons registration). So the native per-call growth is still open at HEAD.

Corrections:
1. "Over half of the tick by round 33+" is overstated. From 02:07 (r32) to the end, SV_UnitAlive was 33-58% of the tick, median about 46%. It was over 50% in only 6 of 24 five-minute periods (02:07, 02:17, 02:42, 03:08, 03:23, 03:44). It is still the largest single cost.
2. The growth is with the units on the phase's list, not every unit ever spawned. A unit stays on the list until it is spawned again or recycled. At r44, 40 of the 57 entries had 0 alive (pool flights, Ladons, LCACs, VALKA, the Anomaly).
3. The finding is wrong about HEAD's leave probe. At HEAD (99209a3, WIP, not yet run in game) sv_core.lua:422 reads `local every = LEAVE.why and 1 or 5`: every 5 s, not twice a second. The same commit also:
   - makes the allies' share ask each unit every 4 s and has airUp read ALLY.alive;
   - sends the director's asks through ALIVE;
   - checks co-op's unlinked units every 10 s;
   - takes special units with nothing alive off the list (SPC.recycleLater: Ladon, VALKA, the Anomaly, LCAC lanes, the Spaceport's units).
   In this run that would remove about 10 of the 57 entries, leaving roughly 47 at about 1.85 ms a call. ALIVE still asks 8-32 times a second, so a late long run at HEAD would still spend roughly 4-6 ms a tick here.

So the interim leave-probe fix the finding proposes is already done at HEAD. The native root cause is not fixed.
verdicts.corrected_status: KNOWN (R30_FINDINGS perf, now seen in solo too) and still open at HEAD in the native runtime: per-call cost of about 0.65 ms plus 26 µs per list entry. HEAD's Lua already reduces it (99209a3, not yet run in game): fewer asks (leave probe every 5 s, allies' share every 4 s, airUp and the director through cached answers) and special units with nothing alive taken off the list. The finding's interim fix for the leave probe is therefore superseded. Its share of the tick late in the run was 33-58% (median about 46%), not consistently over half.
verdicts.fix:
A native-only fix in runtime/survival_rt.c that keeps the "on the phase's list" meaning:
(1) Keep a small table: unit UniqueID → unit pointer. Fill it from Spawn (the pointer g_spawnUnit returns, once RegisteredUnit has confirmed it) and from any hit in a full RegisteredUnit walk. In RegisteredUnit, when a cached pointer exists, first look for that pointer in PhaseUnits()->data by plain pointer comparison. This does not dereference the other entries, so there is no VirtualQuery or virtual call per entry (about 100 ns for 57 entries). On a match, confirm it with one Readable plus UnitId(u) == id, because a freed pointer can be reused. Fall back to today's full walk only when there is no cached pointer or it is not found.
(2) Cache the desc pointer per FName (FindDesc) and the offsets of UnitDescList and AliveChildAIGameObjects, each resolved once per level or class, instead of a U.valuePtr name lookup on every call.
(3) Clear both caches in Recycle (after g_unregisterUnit), in TeardownClose / when the gate closes, and when FindSpawner switches g_phase / g_wd.
This makes a call O(1) apart from the pointer compare, and should also cut most of the 0.65 ms fixed part. Nothing more is needed in Lua for the leave probe: HEAD already asks every 5 s.

verdicts.reason:
The finding holds. I re-derived the numbers myself, from every one of the 78 'perf: lists' lines in the solo log and from the native log's per-round 'units (round N ...)' lists. Three details are wrong or out of date.

What I confirmed (c_casual44, 0.73.78, runtime 0.32.23):
- Calls and cost per call rise together. At r1 (21:35:15) it is 2.1 calls a tick and 1.53 ms (0.73 ms a call). At r10 (23:12:16) 3.8 calls and 4.60 ms. At r20 (00:13:33) 3.4 calls and 5.96 ms. At r33 (02:17:17) 7.8 calls and 15.51 ms. At r39 (03:23:40) 7.6 calls and 16.22 ms of a 28.0 ms tick (2.13 ms a call).
- The cost per call follows the length of the phase's list: 0.6-1.0 ms with 1-10 units, 1.2-1.3 ms with 20-22, 1.65-1.75 ms with 34-37, 1.9-2.2 ms with 51-58. That is about 0.7 ms fixed plus about 23 us a unit on this PC.
- In the 0.73.81 co-op run (d_alessia) it is 0.66 ms a call (12:45, about 2 units) up to 2.86 ms (13:26, about 31 units reconstructed from the spawn and recycle lines). That is about 70 us a unit on her PC, the same as R30's 75 us.
- The other numbers are right: the list grows from 1 to 57-58 units, there are 401 recycles, 'leave check' goes 1.3 -> 6.4 ms, allies/counts 0.2 -> 2.9 ms, and d_alessia makes 1.1-3.0 calls a tick, 5.20 ms / 2.0 at 13:21.
- The code is as described. UnitAlive (runtime/survival_rt.c:1517) calls SpawnerReady, then FindDesc (a valuePtr lookup of UnitDescList and a walk over the descs), then RegisteredUnit (:1378). RegisteredUnit walks the whole list, and each entry costs Readable() (one VirtualQuery) plus UnitId, which does a second Readable/VirtualQuery and a virtual call. Then UnitArrayNum does another valuePtr. `git diff 294712f HEAD -- runtime/survival_rt.c` (11 lines) changes none of this, so the native part is still open at HEAD.

Corrections:
1. "Over half of the tick by round 33+" overstates it. From r33 on, the share is 33-58% (median about 45%), and above 50% in only 5 of the 23 windows (the peak is 03:23, 58%). It is the largest single cost, not the majority.
2. "The more units have ever been spawned" is wrong. Recycle takes a desc's old unit off the list before it spawns again, so the list holds one entry per distinct unit desc. It levelled off at 57-58 from r38, against 865 spawns and 401 recycles, and the cost per call levelled off at about 2.0 ms from r32. At round 44 the list was:
   - 25 pool flights at 0 alive
   - 11 defence units
   - 6 allied units
   - about 11 specials' units (2 Ladons, 4 LCAC units plus 1 troop unit, VALKA x2, MINDRIPPER (SV_Unit_Anomaly) x2)
   - 4 stock or pad units
3. "The leave probe asks twice a second at HEAD" is out of date. HEAD's commit 99209a3 (WIP 0.73.83, not yet in a build or run in game) asks every 5 s (`local every = LEAVE.why and 1 or 5`, sv_core.lua:422). The same commit:
   - asks for each allied unit every 4 s (SHARE 16)
   - has airUp read the kept counts
   - sends the director through ALIVE
   - runs co-op's unit check every 10 s
   - takes the specials' units off the list after their round (SPC.recycleLater)

   So the proposed Lua stopgap is already done at HEAD.

What that leaves at HEAD, estimated for this run: about 46 of the 57 units stay on the list (the pool, the defences, the allies). ALIVE still asks each watched unit about once a second (8-32 asks a second). My rough estimate is 3.5-4.5 calls a tick at about 1.8 ms, so 6-8 ms a tick instead of 16. That is about half, but still the largest native cost. The status stays known-open: partly mitigated in HEAD's WIP Lua, with the native cost unfixed.
verdicts.corrected_status: known-open (still the largest native cost at HEAD; HEAD's WIP commit 99209a3 already makes the Lua side ask less and takes the specials' units off the list; the native walk is unchanged)
verdicts.fix:
Native, the next full build (runtime/survival_rt.c):
- RegisteredUnit (:1378): drop the two VirtualQuery calls per entry. PhaseUnits already checks a->data readable for num*8 in one call. Keep a small cache of unique id -> unit pointer, filled by Spawn and by a successful walk, and cleared in Recycle (:1398), at the teardown gate and when the world changes. On a hit, check that the pointer is still in a->data with plain pointer compares (about 57, no syscall) and that UObjLive(unit) == 1, then return it without UnitId. Only a miss does the full walk.
- The fixed ~0.7 ms: keep the offsets of UnitDescList (FindDesc) and AliveChildAIGameObjects (UnitArrayNum) once a level instead of calling U.valuePtr on every call. Keep each name's desc pointer for the level too (FNameRaw -> desc).

This takes SV_UnitAlive from O(list) syscalls to about O(1).

Lua: nothing more is needed for the leave probe. HEAD already asks it every 5 s (99209a3).

Check it in the next log: the 'perf: lists' natives line, where SV_UnitAlive's ms per call should stay flat (under ~0.2 ms) as rounds go on. Turn on [log] verbose once to get the 'units (round N start)' list sizes.

findings.title: VOID WATCHER's ESM field list grows by one each launch and is never pruned; every field is re-read every tick
findings.evidence:
From 'perf: lists': 'ESM fields' goes 10 (23:37) → 22 (r16-23, with no VOID WATCHER up), then 53 (01:41), 122 (02:42), 148 (03:03), 181 (04:04). It never falls, even after 'VOID WATCHER 1 home after 3 rounds ... SV_Recycle 1' (6 times).

SV_ObjChain calls a tick track it: 25 (r1), 40 (23:37), 148 (01:41), 269 (02:42), 403 (03:59).

The 'allies/VOID WATCHER' sub-part goes 0.3 → 2.1 ms a tick, worst 26-38 ms.

Only 2 'ESM field ... new' lines and no 'launched again (pooled' line: every launch made a new field.
findings.cause: sv_allies.lua L1138-1167 (HEAD): fields from NotifyOnNewObject are added to R.esmFields and dropped only when liveAddr/nameOf says the object is gone. These fields stay live UObjects. Every awacsTick does liveAddr + nameOf (GetFullName) + bHidden + EffectRangeMeter reads for each of them. R30 suggested 'look at the ESM fields only on an ESM launch'; that isn't built.
findings.fix: Prune an entry once its field has been hidden for more than life_s + 5 s after a launch, and clear R.esmFields when VOID WATCHER is taken off (RE_SV_AwacsRemove / its SV_Recycle). Or scan the fields only for ~3 s after each RE_SV_AwacsEsm.

verdicts.reason:
I could not refute it: the logs and the code both confirm it, and nothing after the build that ran has changed it. The status is wrong, though. It is not new: R30 already reported it, and it is still open at HEAD.

Logs (c_casual44/AC8SurvivalMode_lua.log, the `perf: lists:` lines):
- 'ESM fields' runs 10 (23:37:48, L3522), 17, then 22 (23:48:00, L3926). It stays at exactly 22 from 23:48 to 01:10:43 (L6478), when no VOID WATCHER was up: it was taken off at 23:50:31 (L4039) and recycled at 23:50:33 (L4041), and the next one was bought at 01:14:37 (L6549).
- It then rises by +26, +23, +36, +41 and +32 over the next five services: 48, 71, 107, 148, 180. It ends at 181 (04:04:32, L16580).
- It never falls across 6 'home after 3 rounds ... SV_Recycle 1' lines.
- 'SV_ObjChain N a tick' runs 25 (L431), 40, 148, 269, 403 (03:59:25, L16318), then 23 after the run (L16720). That is about 2.07 calls per field per tick: (403-30)/180.
- 'allies/VOID WATCHER' was 0.0 before the purchase and 0.3 ms with 22 fields and no VOID WATCHER up (23:58-01:10). It was 1.6-1.8 ms with 148 fields and no VOID WATCHER up (03:08-03:23), and 2.0-2.2 ms with 168-181 fields. The average cost therefore follows the list size, not VOID WATCHER's activity.
- Each service added about 0.7-0.85 fields per 30-s ESM launch. For example, the first service ran 23:33:04 to 23:45:56, about 26 launches, for +22 fields.
- There is no 'launched again (pooled' line in this log, nor in the two other logs that show the counter (65 fields in a_31round, 4 in d_alessia). esmSet always logs the first two re-launches, so in 4.5 h no field was ever detected as re-launched. The loop's whole purpose never fired.
- One nuance: '2 new lines' is not evidence. esmSet logs only the first 2 new fields by design.
- A second nuance: the 'worst 26-38 ms' comes mostly from VOID WATCHER being up, not from the list. It was already 24-26 ms at 10-22 fields while up, but 3-8 ms with 22 fields while down. It was 20-21 ms with 148 fields while down.

Code: there is no diff in this code between 294712f (0.73.78, the build that ran) and HEAD (2c277d4).
- sv_allies.lua:1145-1171 adds every BP_wp_esm_MS28_C from NotifyOnNewObject. The class is already filtered on insert.
- Every awacsTick then runs, for each entry: liveAddr (one SV_ObjChain call), nameOf (a second SV_ObjChain call plus GetFullName), a bHidden read and an EffectRangeMeter read.
- An entry is dropped only when liveAddr or nameOf says the object is gone. These pooled fields stay in GUObjectArray, which was found (AC8SurvivalMode.log L39), so they are never dropped.
- Nothing clears R.esmFields. The loss path at sv_allies.lua:1251 clears `R.awacsFields = {}`, a stale name from 0.73.33 (3375a47) that 0.73.73 (734e0ce) replaced without updating this line.
- awacsService's removal path (around L888) clears nothing.

Status: R30_FINDINGS.json /0/findings/8 already reported this as part of the 'allies / coop / VOID WATCHER' growth finding: "'allies/VOID WATCHER' 0.6 -> 1.8 while 'ESM fields' went 9 -> 60 ... look at the ESM fields only on an ESM launch". None of R30's proposed fixes for it were built in 0.73.80, 0.73.81, 0.73.82 or the WIP commits after them, so it is KNOWN and still open at HEAD.
verdicts.corrected_status: KNOWN (R30 /0/findings/8 sub-item: ESM fields 9 -> 60, allies/VOID WATCHER 0.6 -> 1.8 ms) and still open at HEAD; this solo run shows it unbounded (181 fields, about 2.1 ms a tick, about 370 SV_ObjChain calls a tick).
verdicts.fix:
Smallest fix at HEAD, all in sv_allies.lua:

1. Fix the stale name at line 1251: `if s.ally == "awacs" then R.awacsFields = {} end` should be `R.esmFields, R.esmOrder = {}, {}`. Clear them the same way in awacsService's removal, right after `R.up[u], RUN.dirty = nil, true` (around line 888).

2. Cap the list, because clearing alone doesn't cover joiners: their R.up never holds the host's VOID WATCHER. In the insert (lines 1146-1153), append the address to R.esmOrder. While #R.esmOrder > 8, set R.esmFields[table.remove(R.esmOrder, 1)] = nil. No field was ever re-launched in any of the logs (0 'launched again' lines at 181, 65 and 4 fields), and 0.73.73's pool was two fields, so the 8 newest cover any reuse.

3. Optional: in the per-entry loop (lines 1156-1171), check `nameOf(e.obj) ~= e.name` only once a second rather than on every tick. GetFullName plus the second SV_ObjChain is about half of each entry's cost.

The cost is then bounded at about 0.1 ms a tick and 16 SV_ObjChain calls a tick, whatever the run length.

verdicts.reason:
The evidence checks out in c_casual44/AC8SurvivalMode_lua.log, the cause is right, and HEAD has not fixed it. The status is wrong, though, and the analyst's first two fixes are unsafe.

Log numbers, re-checked:
- 'ESM fields' on the perf: lists lines: 10 (L3522, 23:37:48), 17 (23:42:54), then 22 at every line from 23:48:00 to 01:10:43, when no VOID WATCHER was up. Then 24 (01:15:58), 53 (01:41:31), 122 (02:42:48), 148 at every line from 03:03:15 to 03:23:40 (none up: home at 03:05:01, next bought 03:26:01), and 181 at 04:04:32 (L16580).

- SV_ObjChain per tick: 25 (21:35), 40 (23:37), 148 (01:41), 269 (02:32 and 02:42), 403 (03:59). (403-23)/180 is about 2.1 calls per field per tick. That matches the loop's liveAddr plus nameOf, which each call SV_ObjChain once; nameOf also does a GetFullName.
- 'allies/VOID WATCHER': 0.0 through round 12, 0.3 ms at 22 fields (no VOID WATCHER up), 1.6-1.8 ms at 148 fields with none up, 2.0-2.2 ms at about 180 fields (03:38-04:04). Worst 20-38 ms. That is about 2 of the second tick half's 7-8 ms.
- No 'launched again (pooled' line in this run.
- The point 'only 2 new lines' is not evidence. esmSet (sv_allies.lua:851) logs only the first two new fields. The count is what proves the growth.

Code: the field loop in ALLY.awacsTick (HEAD sv_allies.lua:1156-1171) is identical in 294712f (0.73.78) and at HEAD; I diffed that region and it matches. The loop runs every tick whether a VOID WATCHER is up or not. It drops an entry only when liveAddr or nameOf says the object is gone, and these fields stay live. No commit on any branch changes it after a2edaa9. 0.73.83's WIP (99209a3) changed only allies/counts.

Status correction: this is not new. R30_FINDINGS.json, finding 'Host allies, coop and VOID WATCHER parts grow the same way', already had it: "'allies/VOID WATCHER' 0.6 -> 1.8 while 'ESM fields' went 9 -> 60 ... the pooled fields are never dropped while live". Its fix ("look at the fields only within a few seconds of an ESM launch") was never built. Correct status: KNOWN, still open at HEAD. The 44-round run shows it reaching 181 fields and about 2 ms a tick.

The fix as proposed is partly unsafe. The game does reuse old fields. In R30's host log (testing/logs/2026-11-04/r30_host_SaintAlessia/AC8SurvivalMode_lua.log), VOID WATCHER was lost at 19:51:14 and a new one bought at 19:52:54. That new one launched two existing fields again, at 19:53:48 and 19:54:48 ("launched again (pooled; 1/2 so far) ... range 9000.0 -> 9000.0 m, life 10000.0 -> 15.0 s"). The count stayed flat at 33 from 19:50:56 to 19:56:06.
- So clearing R.esmFields when VOID WATCHER is taken off, or pruning fields hidden for life_s + 5 s, would miss such relaunches. A missed field would keep the game's life of 10000 s and support range of 8000 m, which is the 0.73.73 regression again.
- That relaunch also shows EffectRangeMeter left at 9000, so the 'theirs' range test can't see it. Only the shown/hidden edge or LifeTime does.

The analyst's third option, a scan window after each launch, is the safe one (see fix).
verdicts.corrected_status: KNOWN (R30's finding on the allies / coop / VOID WATCHER parts growing; its fix, a scan only after a launch, was never built), still open at HEAD; minor perf
verdicts.fix:
Run the field loop only for a few seconds after each ESM launch, and spot a launch by its LifeTime as well as its shown/hidden state. Don't prune fields or clear the list.
(1) sv_allies.lua:1129, after `local r = SV_Event(aw.esm.event)`: `R.esmScanUntil = now + 3; R.esmScanFresh = true`.
(2) A joiner fires the host's forwarded event in sv_coop.lua hostEvent (around :1529, after `local r = rawEvent(name)`): `if name == CFG.allies.awacs.esm.event then ALLY.esmScanSoon = true end`. 1. In ALLY.repairAll (sv_allies.lua:716):

verdicts.reason:
Confirmed from the logs and the code, at the build the log ran and at HEAD.

**Logs**

e_loose UE4SS.log (0b8e0fb2-UE4SS.log):
- L1107, 06:24:44.6756: "mission restarted in round 1 (SV_Beat 6 -> 0)". LB.finish runs right after it: "leaderboard: run over (restart) ... not sent: SP OFFLINE" at .6793.
- The same tick, still on the old D:
  - L1114, .6818: "round 1: 0 aircraft in 0 flights left". At 06:24:11 the round had 4 aircraft in 2 flights, and the player had 0 kills.
  - L1115: "round 1 clear; round 2 in 20 s"
  - L1116: "credits: +250 (round 1 cleared), now 250"
  - L1117, .6871: "hud: callout 'ROUND 1 COMPLETE'"
  - then the kills line and, at .7180, "allies: repaired between rounds".
- At .7945, "intensity: round 1: you avg 7 ..." is logged by DIR.tick in the tick's second half (probeTickB, about 125 ms later). So the second half also runs on the old D.
- At .9198, "level loaded" (the reset on the next tick). The new run starts at 0 Z: L1166, 06:25:31, "+100 ..., now 100".
- The real round 1 clear comes later, at L1188-1190 (06:26:25).

c_casual44 UE4SS.log L17386-17388, 04:08:16.932: three "mission restarted in round 44" lines in one tick (SV_Kills 332->0, SV_AirHits 279->0, SV_Beat 2174->0). LB.finish is called 3 times, but its `st.ended` guard (sv_leaderboard.lua:639) makes the extra calls no-ops. The run had already ended by death at 04:08:10 and was sent with a 200. So there it is only a duplicated log line. No fake clear shows in that tick.

Only these two sessions have a restart.

**Code**

The restart branch is the same in 294712f (0.73.78, sv_main.lua:530) and at HEAD (2c277d4; working tree clean). `git log -S` shows it hasn't changed since the Lua split. At HEAD, sv_main.lua:523-537 only sets `levelTick = -1` ("the level-load reset below, on the next tick") and calls LB.finish inside the per-flag loop, with no break. Then sv_main.lua:541-588 run, for the same tick on the old D: roundsTick, hudTick, musicTick, the music hold, airfieldTick and bombTick. `bNow, bPaused = now, paused` then hands the round clock to probeTickB, which runs shop, allies, hits, tactical, the director and ammo 125 ms later.

The reset itself is in probeTick:401-460, on the next tick. After the mission reload the units are gone, so the "fighting" branch (sv_rounds.lua:1647-1704) counts 0 and clears the round: SPC.endTick / ko.over, addCredits, hudCallout, ALLY.repairAll.

At HEAD, ALIVE.ask's cache (answers up to 1 s old, 0.73.80) can make the fake clear depend on timing, but nothing guards against it. In a "wave" or "spawning" state, the same leftover tick could start a wave or call SV_Spawn into the reloading mission.

**Impact**

In solo it is cosmetic. D, RUN, callouts and H are all replaced on the next tick, and LB.finish has already recorded the run. There is one small exposure: a FindAllOf-type walk (repairAll) runs during the mission reload.

In co-op the host's addCredits wrapper would also send the "cr" round bonus and the "co" callout to joiners (sv_coop.lua:5333-5355). That path was not seen in any log, and the joiners' newRunHere likely wipes it.

**Corrections to the finding**

- Severity minor and status NEW are right.
- The finding's fix is incomplete. `if now and not restarted then` still leaves `bNow = now`, so the second half still runs on the dead D.
verdicts.corrected_status: new (confirmed; open at HEAD 2c277d4)
verdicts.fix:
In sv_main.lua probeTick (HEAD L516-540), stop the leftover tick once a restart is seen. Do it with one log line and one LB.finish:

```lua
local restarted = false
if tick % 8 == 4 then
    local f = svFlags()
    if f then
        D.maxFlags = D.maxFlags or {}
        for _, k in ipairs({ "SV_Kills", "SV_AirHits", "SV_Beat" }) do
            local v = f[k]
            if v then
                if not restarted and (D.maxFlags[k] or 0) > 0 and v < D.maxFlags[k] then
                    restarted = true
                    log(... "mission restarted ..." ...)
                    levelTick = -1
                    local okL, errL = pcall(LB.finish, "restart")
                    if not okL then log("leaderboard: error " .. tostring(errL)) end
                end
                D.maxFlags[k] = math.max(D.maxFlags[k] or 0, v)
            end
        end
    end
end
```

Then, right after `perfAdd("restart check", tRc)`:

```lua
if restarted then
    -- the dead run's rounds / HUD / pay not ticked; the reset comes next tick
    bNow, bPaused, CLOCK_TICK, CLOCK_PAUSED = nil, nil, nil, nil
    return
end
```

This skips roundsTick, hud, music, the music hold, airfield and bombers in this half. Clearing bNow also skips the second half's now-gated parts: shop, allies, icons, sound, hits, tactical, tells and tail watch. The analyst's `if now and not restarted` alone leaves bNow set.

Optionally add a lua check that feeds svFlags a dropped SV_Beat with D.state "fighting" and no units alive, and asserts that no "round N clear" or credits line is logged before the level-load reset.

So the proposed `if now and not restarted` fix covers the e_loose case but not this window.

Severity minor: the next tick's reset throws away D, RUN (newRun) and the HUD (H.widget:RemoveFromParent).
verdicts.fix:
sv_main.lua at HEAD:

(1) Restart loop (L527-534): on the first dropped flag, log, set levelTick = -1, call LB.finish once, then set `restarted = true` and `break`.

(2) Right after `perfAdd("restart check", tRc)` (L543), add: `if levelTick == -1 then bNow, bPaused = nil, nil; return end`. This also covers a new Survival World that set levelTick = -1 during the tick. Nothing of the dead run then runs in that tick: no rounds, HUD, music, airfield or bombers.

(3) In probeTickB, after its leave check (L613), add: `if levelTick == -1 then return end`. That stops the STORE, allies, hits and loggers running on the dead D in the second half.

(4) Optional: change the restart check's gate from `tick % 8 == 4` (L523) to every tick. svFlags already caches its read for 1 s, so this adds no walks. It cuts the window before detection from up to 2 s to about 1 s; that window is where e_loose's ammo put-back happened.

critic.summary:
I found six new findings. None of them repeats the four analysts or R30_FINDINGS.json. They come from log classes nobody explained: other mods' lines in UE4SS.log, the one "no STORE row TextBlock" line in every session, the TESTER missile-outcome totals, the joiner's stand-in backstop lines, the joiner's "NOT removed" Alicorn line and the joiner's native guard counters.

1. **Leaderboard ranked a run played with a gameplay mod (major).** Saint Alessia hosted both co-op runs with AC8TLSHoming running, among 9 other UE4SS mods. That mod gives the TLS 25 shots instead of 20, a 12 s beam instead of 10 s, beam steering onto targets and its own damage values. Survival logged "you fired sp1" before 127 of her roughly 282 own kills, and the server accepted run 63121574 with a 200. LB.edited and the build hash never look at other mods. The 0.73.81 run was kept for resending, so it will rank as soon as hash 732e9119 is registered.

2. **STORE label update falls back to scanning every TextBlock for the whole session (minor, perf).** This is the root cause behind D20. All five sessions log the fallback line exactly once, on the first approach or landing, before any STORE page is open. A relabel runs whenever the player is near the airfield (within 3 km, under 100 m). With no menu up it finds no row TextBlock and switches to the slow path permanently. From then on each label update reads all ~1,065 TextBlocks with nothing cached: 43 to 159 walks per session, 1.6 to 4.9 s in total. The 0.73.77 kept-rows path never ran in any log.

3. **The TESTER missile-outcome logger reports almost no hits (minor, logger bug).** It counted 3 hits of 659 missiles at the host in the 31-round run and 4 of 205 in the 0.73.81 run. In the same windows the host's death record shows 5 missile hits, and the hit logger shows missiles 21 to 50 m away at the moment of damage. Two causes: missiles are sampled every 0.5 s against a 150 m hit radius, so the last sample before impact is usually too far out, and ally ESM and enemy ECM fields are counted as missiles at you.

4. **The stand-ins' "damage-0" rows still do damage (minor, desync).** On Rapt0r's game, copies took 14 to 149 HP from the host's and dukka's F-16C stand-ins 200 or more times. The backstop kept that damage from being sent to the host. A copy left above the 1 HP floor keeps the lowered health on the joiner until the host's next health update.

5. **The joiner never removes its copy of the Alicorn (minor, perf).** The joiner's check ran about 13 s before the host's RE_SV_AlcnRemove reached it and logged "NOT removed (204 alive)". No later check or recycle exists on a joiner, so the hull and its 181 parked pool planes stay on the joiner's spawner list. HEAD still has this.

6. **The native guards caught a burst on the joiner, with no crash (info, confirmed working).** 1,555 dead target entries and 298 freed-object events were caught in 0.6 s. They came 0.36 s after the 30-s-deferred destroy of a recycled Tu-160 flight's unit actor, which shows the delay does not let the engine drop its references. Host and solo logs show zero.

I checked and left out several things: the working-set collapse and the host's other mods' frame cost (R30 already has them), the joiner's red sky and song for VALKA (R30 already confirmed it), the early-window specials not counting toward the max_gap (a design choice), the HUD widget counter doubling on restart (a cosmetic counter) and the "19 of 9 aircraft" line (cosmetic).

findings.title: Ranked co-op runs were played with a gameplay-changing UE4SS mod (AC8TLSHoming: more TLS ammo, longer beam, beam steering, own damage), and nothing in LB.edited or the build hash sees other mods
findings.sessions: a_31round (host), d_alessia (host); b_Logs / e_loose / c_casual44 for comparison
findings.evidence: a_31round/UE4SS.log: "Mod 'AC8TLSHoming' has enabled.txt, starting mod" (09:52:42) next to 8 other mods (AC8CockpitFreedom, AC8ModSettings, AC8UltrawideHUD, FovMod, SkinSlotText, SkinStudioSaveBackup, falken-us4ss, IoStoreLoaderMod). Its lines: "Loaded v0.6.8; all TLS subclasses; beamSteering=true"; "TLS_AMMO_SOURCE ... DT_PlayerParameter_PP9001_falken_L001 row=falken weaponId=28 levels=31 changed=62 bonus=5"; "TLS_AMMO_NATIVE_SOURCE original=20 bonus=5 capacity=25"; "TLS_DURATION_PREPARED base=10.0000s bonus=2.0000s duration=12.0000s" (TLS_DURATION_BONUS_ACTIVE 105x); "TLS_DAMAGE_APPLIED initial=55.0000 tick=20.0000 interval=0.4000s". In total: 1,267 lines, 77 BEAM_START, 32 BEAM_VERIFY 'turned=true', 29 BEAM_BONUS_VERIFY with nativeTarget=<enemy plane>. The TLS is Survival's special 1: at 10:11:11.357 "ammo: ... special 1 25 -> 11" and "TLS_AMMO_CHANGED index=3 previous=25 current=11" are 6 ms apart. Of the host's ~282 own kill lines (those with no teammate or ally credit following), 127 have "you fired sp1" in the 6 s before. The leaderboard sent them anyway: 12:04:58 "Saint Alessia (host) 304/33/1", 12:05:02 "server answered 200: {\"ok\":true,\"score\":209700}". d_alessia/UE4SS.log: the same mod set (742 AC8TLSHoming lines, 79 BEAM_START). That run was refused only as an unknown build (13:27:11, 422) and is "kept to resend ... for 14 days ... register this build's hash on /admin and it's taken". The joiner Rapt0r (b) and Copperpug (e) ran only IoStoreLoaderMod. Nada (c) ran AC8UnitHealth, which only displays ("READY v0.1.4: enemy and friendly health below native unit names").
findings.cause: sv_leaderboard.lua LB.edited (HEAD :116-144) checks only CFG against CFG_DEFAULTS, a survival_config.lua and test keys. runtime/build_hash.c (:241) hashes only Survival's own mod folder and container. Nothing enumerates the other UE4SS mods that UE4SS starts from enabled.txt ("Starting mods (from enabled.txt ...)").
findings.fix: At game start, list the UE4SS mods that are on. Natively: a small SV_Mods() using FindFirstFileW over Mods\*\enabled.txt. In Lua as a minimum: io.open on a denylist of Mods\<name>\enabled.txt (AC8TLSHoming, SPWeaponCustomizer, AC8WeaponSwap, AC8WeaponValues). Log the list. LB.edited adds "mod <name>" for any mod not on a display-only allowlist (IoStoreLoaderMod, FovMod, AC8UltrawideHUD, SkinSlotText, SkinStudioSaveBackup, AC8ModSettings, AC8UnitHealth), and the run JSON carries the list so the Worker can refuse it. Hold off registering hash 732e9119 until this decision is made, or the kept 0.73.81 run ranks.

findings.title: STORE label updates scan every TextBlock for the whole session: an empty-menu update near the airfield switches them to the slow path permanently, and the 0.73.77 kept-rows path never runs
findings.sessions: all five (a_31round, b_Logs, d_alessia, c_casual44, e_loose)
findings.evidence: Every session logs "shop: no STORE row TextBlock under a WBP_Menu_Text_Focus row; row labels are looked for in every TextBlock" exactly once, at the first airfield visit and before any STORE page is up. a: 10:10:54 (gear down 10:10:48, on the ground 10:11:01). d: 12:54:12 (gear down 12:54:10, on the ground 12:54:19). b: 12:13:22 (on the ground 12:13:16, 'track clock held (landing store)' only at 12:13:24). c: 22:16:47, together with 'spawns held while you are down at the airfield'. e: 06:32:59. The kept-rows line "shop: the STORE rows' N TextBlocks kept for its labels" appears 0 times in all five logs. TextBlock walks in the perf 'lists' lines: a 125 walks / 4,940 ms, b 159 / 4,337 ms, c 111 / 2,755 ms, d 43 / 1,564 ms; b 12:55:16 'TextBlock 5x 134 ms (1065 found)'.
findings.cause: sv_shop.lua SHOP.relabelFlush (HEAD ~:497) runs whenever playerOnAirfield() is true. That function (sv_rounds.lua:1346-1351) means within 3 km and under 100 m, so it is true on final approach and right after touchdown. Labels are queued whenever a price changes, which in co-op includes teammates' kills, round bonuses and room counts. With no landing menu up, relabel() (sv_shop.lua ~:453-488) finds no WBP_Menu_Text_Focus TextBlock and at :484 sets SH.relabelAll = true, which never resets. In 'all' mode the list is never kept (:470 requires `not all`), so every later relabel runs FindAllOf("TextBlock") and GetText():ToString() on about 1,000 widgets. The code is the same in 0.73.79 (294712f) and at HEAD.
findings.fix: Don't set relabelAll when no landing window is shown: in relabel, if rows == 0 and SHOP.windowsKey(SH.tick) == "", return nil (the queue is kept and retried) instead of latching. Also return early from relabelFlush unless landingWindows() holds a STORE page, and clear SH.relabelAll at each landing.

findings.title: The TESTER missile-outcome logger misses almost every hit (3 of 659 at the host) and counts ally ESM and enemy ECM fields as missiles at you
findings.evidence: a: run totals at the end of the 'missiles at you' lines: 659 missiles, 3 hit, 0 decoyed. At 10:21:23 the death record says "missiles 100% (5 hits from 1 shooters, 5 brackets)", backed by hit lines at 10:21:16 (-30 HP, BP_wp_msl_r0 20 m from BP_OP1027_m21b_CP), 10:21:20 (-22), 10:21:21 (-45 in 2 hits) and 10:21:23 (-7). The logger's next window at 10:22:05 says "BP_wp_msl_r0 9 (0 hit, 0 decoyed, 9 missed)". d: hit lines with a missile close at the moment of damage: 13:15:21 hcaa 42 m, 13:18:42 msl_r0 21 m, 13:22:03 laam_r0 33 m, 13:25:24 and 13:25:25 2aam 25 and 50 m. Yet the 13:27:00 run totals say "BP_wp_hcaa_r0 6 (0 hit ...)", "BP_wp_msl_r0 33 (0 hit", "BP_wp_laam_r0 18 (0 hit", "BP_wp_2aam_a0 21 (0 hit". The same totals list "BP_wp_esm_MS28 65 (0 hit, 0 decoyed, 65 missed)" (a), which is VOID WATCHER 1's own ally ESM, and "BP_wp_ecm_a0 15 (1 hit ...)" (d).
findings.cause: sv_weaponlog.lua settle (HEAD :153-156) counts a hit only if t.minM <= hit_m (150 m) and the health drop is within 1.2 s. minM is sampled only once each every_s (0.5 s, :276), and a missile closing at several hundred m/s is last seen 150-450 m out before it disappears, so a real hit is logged as 'missed'. :344 tracks any weapon whose owner kind isn't 'you' or 'none' and whose TargetToHome is your pawn, so LiveElectronicWeaponBase fields and allied weapons are counted too.
findings.fix: Count a hit when the drop falls within ~0.6 s of goneAt and the last sampled distance is within hit_m + closing speed × every_s (keep the previous sample to get the speed). Alternatively, attribute each health drop to the nearest tracked missile that vanished within ±0.6 s. Leave the LiveElectronicWeaponBase base and ally-owned weapons out of the outcomes.

findings.title: The stand-ins' damage-0 rows still do damage: copies on a joiner lost 14-149 HP to other players' AI stand-ins 200+ times
findings.evidence: b 12:03:13 "coopfire: the stand-ins' damage-0 rows: 31 of 31 airframes"; 12:08:26 "player 1's plane as f16c_common_svcp: spawned" and the same for player 2 (both flew the Falken, which has no player blueprint on his game). Then 12:16:37 "coopfire: copy 78 lost 74.0, 74.0 of it another player's stand-in's here: nothing sent (1 times)" and 12:16:38 "copy 79 lost 149.0 ... (2 times)" (the Tu-95 went down to player 1 at 12:16:40). The counter reaches 50 at 12:53:54, 100 at 13:09:42, 150 at 13:21:53 and 200 at 13:50:54; the line is logged for the first 5 and then every 50th. Losses run 14.3-149 HP.
findings.cause: COOP.syncSetup (sv_coop.lua HEAD ~:3946-4023) zeroes damage and AreaOfEffectDamage on the cloned NpcWeapon rows (<W>_SVCP). The stand-ins' fire, relayed or from their own AI, still puts damage in the copies' DamageHistoryMap, so the projectile's damage evidently does not come from that row. The Ladon sure-kill missile also had to be toned on its instance at launch. The backstop (sv_coop.lua ~:1852-1863) keeps the damage from being sent. A copy left above the floor keeps the lowered health locally (newH = h, ~:1870) until the host's next 'hp', and one knocked to the floor waits there, so the joiner's own hits on it can't show.
findings.fix: Tone the stand-ins' projectiles to 0 damage at launch, the way the Ladon missiles are: from the weapon NotifyOnNewObject feed, when the OwningGameObject is in M.standInSet(), write the instance's damage fields to 0. In addition or instead, after a stand-in-only cut, put the copy's health back to c.exp as allies' copies already are.

findings.title: A joiner checks its Alicorn copy about 13 s before the host's removal reaches it and never removes it: the hull and 181 parked pools stay on the joiner's spawner list
findings.evidence: Clock offset from shared events: the joiner is 1:59:59 ahead ('THE ALICORN IS SINKING' at 11:03:05 host and 13:03:04 joiner; 'ROUND 19 COMPLETE' at 11:03:16 and 13:03:15). Joiner 13:03:10: "the Alicorn's unit (SV_Unit_Alicorn) the host's alicorn over: 204 alive, 23 of its 226 recorded objects still up: 0 finished off, 23 switched off (181 parked pools left to the unit's removal)"; 13:03:12: "special: the Alicorn's unit (SV_Unit_Alicorn) here (a joiner's copies) NOT removed (204 alive)". Host crumbs: 11:03:26.495 'event RE_SV_AlcnRemove: 1' (about 13:03:25 on the joiner, after its check); 11:03:33 'recycle SV_Unit_Alicorn: unregistering its unit actor ... (204 alive)'. The joiner logs nothing more about SV_Unit_Alicorn in the remaining 62 minutes.
findings.cause: sv_rounds.lua SPC.clientClean (HEAD ~:458-470) schedules the joiner's clean-up CLIENT_AFTER_S after the host's special goes 'done'. It ignores AFTER_KIND.alicorn (25 s), which on the host waits for RE_SV_AlcnRemove. SPC.cleanTick (HEAD :313-337) never calls SV_Recycle on a joiner (mortal false). SPC.recycleLater (HEAD :385) only takes units with 0 alive, and recycleUnitsOf has no 'alicorn' kind. The shuttle has its own joiner recycle (C.due ... SV_Recycle(unit, 1)); the Alicorn has none.
findings.fix: In clientClean, use AFTER_KIND[kind] for the joiner's due time. Add an Alicorn entry like the shuttle's: a few seconds after the host's RE_SV_AlcnRemove has run here, SV_Recycle(SPC.alicornUnit, 1) and then clear SPC.alcnPool.

findings.title: Native guards caught a burst on the joiner (1,555 dead target entries, 298 freed event objects, no crash) right at a recycled bomber unit's deferred destroy
findings.sessions: b_Logs (joiner); a_31round, d_alessia, c_casual44, e_loose show 0
findings.evidence: b crumbs: 13:26:22.294 'recycle EA_Unit_01_Air0: unregistering its unit actor F9CC02E20 (0 alive), its destroy deferred' when the host's EA_Unit_01_Air0 (Tu-160s) spawned again (gen 290). Its Tu-160 copies and wings were 'taken down ... forced' at 13:26:43-13:26:49. 13:26:52.296 'destroying its old unit actor F9CC02E20 (deferred 30 s)'. 0.36 s later, on 6 worker threads, the native log shows "guard: a weapon's target search skipped a gone unit's entry 12E47AF810 (class 16 of 37: its actor isn't live; 1024 so far)" and "guard: an event of type 27 not matched: its object at +0x18 (12FCC02020) was freed (class 17 of 37 ...; 256 so far)". Final counters: "so far events not matched for a freed object 298, gone units' entries skipped 1555, faults caught 0". Every other session ends with all of these at 0. The joiner kept playing to round 32.
findings.cause: Target-search entries and type-27 events were still referencing the old unit's objects 30 s after it was unregistered. The [recycle] destroy_after_s delay does not drain those references, and the uobj.h / TgtInstall guards answer for them at the moment of destroy.
findings.fix: No change needed; keep the guards. This adds a data point to R30's burst note: bursts also come at the deferred destroy, not only at the re-spawn.
